Manifestly unitary higher Hilbert spaces
Quan Chen, Giovanni Ferrer, Brett Hungar, David Penneys, and Sean Sanford

Abstract
. Higher idempotent completion gives a formal inductive construction of the n n -category of finite dimensional n n -vector spaces starting with the complex numbers. We propose a manifestly unitary construction of low dimensional higher Hilbert spaces, formally constructing the C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -3-category of 3-Hilbert spaces from Baez’s 2-Hilbert spaces, which itself forms a 3-Hilbert space. We prove that the forgetful functor from 3-Hilbert spaces to 3-vector spaces is fully faithful.



1.
Introduction

An exciting recent development in higher categories is the notion of
higher idempotent completion
for
n
-categories of
[
GJF19
]
(see
[
DR18
]
for
n=2
), and the higher
suspension
operation
\Sigma
.
1
1

1

As we are interested in finite dimensional higher Hilbert spaces, we work here with a fully unital version of higher idempotent and suspension, which is currently not known to be equivalent to the non-unital version.

Starting with
{\mathbb{C}}
,
\Sigma
inductively constructs higher categories of finite dimensional
higher vector spaces
in a completely formal way.
In turn, these higher vector spaces are receptacles for fully extended topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) by the Cobordism Hypothesis
[
BD95
,
Lur09
]
.
For
n=1
,
\Sigma{\mathbb{C}}=\mathsf{Vec}
, the category of finite dimensional vector spaces.
For
n\geq 2
, we define
n\mathsf{Vec}:=\Sigma^{n}{\mathbb{C}}
.
For
n=2
,
we obtain
\Sigma^{2}{\mathbb{C}}=\mathsf{Alg}
, the 2-category of finite dimensional multimatrix algebras, bimodules, and intertwiners,
which is equivalent to
2\mathsf{Vec}
, the 2-category of finite semisimple linear categories, linear functors, and natural tranformations.
One level higher,
we get the 3-category
\mathsf{mFC}
of multifusion categories
[
DSPS20
,
JF22
]
,
which is equivalent to
3\mathsf{Vec}
, the 3-category of finite semisimple 2-categories
[
GJF19
,
Déc22
]
.

(1)

{\mathbb{C}}\xrightarrow{\Sigma}\mathsf{Vec}\xrightarrow{\Sigma}\mathsf{Alg}\simeq 2\mathsf{Vec}\xrightarrow[\text{\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{MR4444089}{}{}]}}]{\Sigma}\mathsf{mFC}\underset{\text{\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{MR4372801}{}{}]}}}{\simeq}3\mathsf{Vec}

One may expect that a fully extended
n
D unitary TQFT should correspond to a notion of finite dimensional
n
-Hilbert space.
In theoretical condensed matter physics, it is widely accepted that higher idempotents describe phase changes between topologically ordered phases of matter
[
Kon14
,
JF22
,
HBJP23
,
KZZZ24
]
.
However, these topological orders are inherently unitary theories, and thus require a unitary version of higher idempotent completion and the suspension operation.
In this article, we propose such an answer up to
n=3
, giving a manifestly unitary construction of finite
2

2

We will investigate infinite dimensional higher Hilbert spaces in future joint work.
higher Hilbert spaces.
Here, the term
unitary
incorporates both the presence of dagger structures at multiple levels, together with positivity conditions.
The former structures were investigated coherently in
[
FHJF+24
]
building on the coherent dagger 1-category treatment in
[
SS23
]
.
In the present paper, we study multiple dagger structures and positivity simultaneously.

In
{\mathrm{B}}\mathsf{Hilb}
, there are several versions of higher idempotent that one might use.
A natural choice which was recently studied in
[
CHPJP22
,
Ver22
]

is the notion of
special standard Q-systems
,
originally defined by
[
Lon94
]
in the context of subfactor theory
[
Lon89
]
,
which are unital separable algebras
(A,\mu,\iota)
such that the adjoint
\mu^{\dagger}
of the multiplication map is an
A-A
bimodule map,

\mu^{\dagger}\mu=\id_{A}
(this is the
special
condition),
and a standardness condition for the maps
1\to A\otimes A
and
A\otimes A\to 1
built from
\mu,\iota
and their adjoints.
In this article, we use the notion of not necessarily special Q-systems, which are exactly the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in the sense of
[
Amb45
]
(see also
[
Bae97
,
HV19
]
).
We thus call them
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
algebras
to avoid any confusion with the higher idempotents studied in
[
CHPJP22
,
Ver22
]
.

Recall that a
2-Hilbert space
in the sense of
[
Bae97
]
is a finite semisimple
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-category
{\mathcal{A}}
equipped with a faithful trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{A}}_{a}:{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a)\to{\mathbb{C}}
for all
a\in{\mathcal{A}}
satisfying some compatibility requirements (see Definition
2.9
below).
The notion of 2-Hilbert space
affords many advantages
and
satisfies certain desiderata
for higher Hilbert spaces.
First, we get a unitary Yoneda embedding

{\mathcal{A}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{A}}^{\op}\to\mathsf{Hilb}),

which was first used in
[
JP17
,
JP19
]
and made explicit in
[
GMP+23
]
.
Second, unitary functors between 2-Hilbert spaces admit unique
unitary adjoints

[
HPT24
]
in the sense that the adjunction natural isomorphisms are unitary:

{\mathcal{B}}(F(a)\to b)\cong^{\dagger}{\mathcal{A}}(a\to F^{*}(b))\qquad\qquad\qquad F\dashv^{\dagger}F^{*}.

In this article, we give a definition of a (finite) 3-Hilbert space.
To present our definition, we introduce the following notions.
First, given a linear 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
with additive hom categories and objects
a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
,
we define the
linking algebra
3
3

3

Here, linking algebra means linking
E_{1}
-algebra in the 2-category
2\mathsf{Vec}
of semisimple categories.

{\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n}):=\bigoplus_{i,j=1}^{n}{\mathfrak{X}}(a_{j}\to a_{i}),

with tensor product defined via matrix multiplication and component-wise composition.
When
{\mathfrak{X}}
is
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
, so is every linking algebra.
Second, for ordinary 2-categories, rigidity (existence of both left and right adjoint 1-morphisms) is a property; any two choices of adjoints are canonically isomorphic.
However, for
\rm C^{*}
2-categories, choosing compatible unitary adjoints over the entire 2-category is a structure, namely that of a
unitary adjoint 2-functor
(which is the identity on objects).
The main difference here is that the canonical isomorphism between distinct choices of adjoints need not be unitary
[
Pen20
]
.

Equipped with the notions of linking algebra and unitary adjoint 2-functor, we make the following definition.

Definition A
.

A
pre-3-Hilbert space
is a linear
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
\mathfrak{X}
such that every linking algebra
is unitary multifusion, equipped with a unitary adjoint 2-functor
\vee
and a
spherical weight

\Psi
, which consists of positive linear maps
\Psi_{a}:\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(1_{a})\to{\mathbb{C}}
for all
a\in{\mathfrak{X}}

satisfying

A 3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a pre-3-Hilbert space that is suitably Cauchy complete, i.e.
{\mathfrak{X}}
admits all
Hilbert direct sums
(a notion defined in
4.2
) and all
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monads in
{\mathfrak{X}}
(defined in
4.3
) split.

The prototypical example of a pre-3-Hilbert space is the delooping
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
of a unitary multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
equipped with a unitary dual functor and a spherical weight
[
Pen20
]
.
We call such a pre-3-Hilbert space an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
multifusion category
.
Our first examples of 3-Hilbert spaces are:

•

the Morita
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}
of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras
[
Amb45
,
Bae97
]
(see also
[
HV19
]
)

•

the
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
2\mathsf{Hilb}
of 2-Hilbert spaces in the sense of
[
Bae97
]
,

As mentioned in Definition
A
, we generalize the notion of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra to an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad in a pre-3-Hilbert space, which gives more examples of 3-Hilbert spaces:

•

the Morita
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
that is additively complete in some unitary sense, and

•

the
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
of unitary modules for a
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
.

We have the following theorem.

Theorem B
.

Every 3-Hilbert space arises as
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
for some
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
.
In particular,
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}})\simeq\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
isometrically as 3-Hilbert spaces.

As an immediate corollary,
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}\simeq 2\mathsf{Hilb}
isometrically as 3-Hilbert spaces.
Thus the notion of
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}(-)
can be viewed as a higher idempotent completion
[
DR18
,
GJF19
,
CHPJP22
,
Ver22
]
which is
manifestly unitary
, fitting in the staircase diagram Figure
1
.

Our second main result is as follows.

Theorem C
.

Taking
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}
is a unitary equivalence between the
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-3-categories
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
and
3\mathsf{Hilb}
which preserves unitary adjoints and spherical weights.
4
4

4

We expect this equivalence is an isometric equivalence of 4-Hilbert spaces (a notion yet to be defined).

As an application, we get the following corollary combining Theorem
C
with
[
Reu23
]
and
[
CGGH23
]
.

Corollary D
.

The forgetful 3-functor
3\mathsf{Hilb}\to 3\mathsf{Vec}
is fully faithful.
5
5

5

The forgetful functor is well-known to not be essentially surjective from the existence of non-unitarizable fusion categories
[
Row05
,
Sch22
]
.

Indeed, the above result follows from commutativity of the following diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{mFC}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 3\mathsf{Hilb}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 3\mathsf{Vec}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}

where
[
Reu23
]
and
[
CGGH23
]
can be used to prove the 3-functor on the top line is fully faithful.

In Figure
1
above, we implicitly claimed that
\Sigma^{\dagger}2\mathsf{Hilb}
is equivalent to
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
.
(This would be the unitary analog of the equivalence

\Sigma 2\mathsf{Vec}\cong\mathsf{mFC}

by
[
Déc23
, Rem. 3.2.9]
using
that multifusion categories in characteristic zero are separable by
[
DSPS20
]
.)
In §
6.2
below, we define a generalizable notion of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}
.
Our final result in this article is as follows.

Theorem E
.

There is an equivalence of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-3-categories
U:{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\cong\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}):|-|

such that
|U({\mathcal{A}})|
is isometrically equivalent to
{\mathcal{A}}
for every
{\mathcal{A}}\in{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}

and

{}_{|U({\mathcal{A}})|}|U({\mathcal{M}})|_{|U({\mathcal{B}})|}
is isometrically equivalent to
{}_{\mathcal{A}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{B}}
for every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
bimodule category.
4

Theorems
C
and
E
together tell us that we may view
3\mathsf{Hilb}
as the unitary suspension of
2\mathsf{Hilb}
.

2.
Background

We note that our treatment of
n
-Hilbert spaces consists only of those which are suitably finite-dimensional.

Notation 2.1
.

In this article, we typically use Roman letters
A,B,C
for sets (possibly with extra structure), caligraphic letters
{\mathcal{A}},{\mathcal{B}},{\mathcal{C}}
for 1-categories (possibly with extra structure), and mathfrak letters
{\mathfrak{A}},{\mathfrak{B}},{\mathfrak{C}}
for 2-categories (possibly with extra structure).
We usually use a sans-serif font for categories and 2-categories with distinct names like
\mathsf{Vec},\mathsf{Hilb},2\mathsf{Vec},2\mathsf{Hilb}
, etc.

2.1.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras and 2-Hilbert spaces

We begin with a rapid treatment of unitary algebras and 2-Hilbert spaces in the sense of
[
Bae97
]
.

A
unitary algebra
is a finite dimensional
\rm C^{*}
-algebra.
A
trace
on a unitary algebra
A
is a linear functional
\Tr:A\to{\mathbb{C}}
satisfying

\Tr(ab)=\Tr(ba)
for all
a,b\in A

and

\Tr(a^{*}a)\geq 0

with equality if and only if
a=0
.
A unitary algebra
A
equipped with a trace
\Tr
gives a Hilbert space
L^{2}(A,\Tr)
via the GNS construction:

\langle a|b\rangle_{L^{2}(A,\Tr)}:=\Tr(a^{*}b).

Since multiplication is bounded on
L^{2}(A,\Tr)
, we get an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
algebra
in the sense of
[
Amb45
]
.

Definition 2.2
.

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
is a unitary algebra
A
equipped with a trace
\Tr_{A}:A\to{\mathbb{C}}
.
We identify
A
with the GNS Hilbert space
L^{2}(A,\Tr_{A})
.

Given an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
(A,\Tr_{A})
and a right action of
A
on a Hilbert space
H
, every
\xi\in H
gives a left creation operator
|\xi\rangle:A_{A}\to H_{A}
by
a\mapsto\xi a
which is manifestly a right
A
-module map.
We denote
|\xi\rangle^{\dagger}
by
\langle\xi|
.
Observe that
\langle\eta|\xi\rangle_{A}\in\End(A_{A})\cong A

gives an
A
-valued inner product.

Definition 2.3
.

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-module
for an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
A
is a Hilbert space
H
equipped with a right
A
-action and a trace
\Tr_{H}\colon\End(H_{A})\to{\mathbb{C}}
satisfying

(2)

\Tr_{H}(|\xi\rangle\langle\eta|)=\Tr_{A}(\langle\eta|\xi\rangle_{A})\qquad\qquad\forall\,\eta,\xi\in H.

We write
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}(A,\Tr_{A})
for the category of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-modules over
(A,\Tr_{A})
with
A
-module maps.

Since
H
is finite dimensional,
\End(H_{A})
is the
A
-compact operators, i.e., the span of the
A
-rank one operators

\left\{|\eta\rangle\langle\xi|\middle|\eta,\xi\in H\right\}
.
Thus
\Tr_{H}
is completely determined by (
2
).
Moreover, we have the identity

\Tr_{A}(\langle\eta|\xi\rangle_{A})=\langle 1_{A}\,|\,\langle\eta|\xi\rangle_{A}\rangle_{L^{2}(A,\Tr_{A})}=\langle\,|\eta\rangle_{A}1_{A}\,|\,|\xi\rangle_{A}1_{A}\rangle_{H}=\langle\eta|\xi\rangle_{H}.

Definition 2.4
.

Given
a,b\in{\mathcal{C}}
in a linear category
{\mathcal{C}}
, the
linking algebra

L(a,b)
is given by formal matrices

\begin{pmatrix}{\mathcal{C}}(a\to a)&{\mathcal{C}}(b\to a)\\
{\mathcal{C}}(a\to b)&{\mathcal{C}}(b\to b)\end{pmatrix},

with product given by matrix multiplication.
(We remind the reader that the columns correspond to the domain, and the rows correspond to the codomain, similar to how a matrix acts as a linear operator.)
When
{\mathcal{C}}
has a dagger structure,
L(a,b)
is a
*
-algebra with
*
being the
{\dagger}
-transpose.
Similarly, we can define the linking algebra

L(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})

for
n
objects
a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\in{\mathcal{C}}
.

Definition 2.5
.

A linear category is called
pre-semisimple
if all
n
-fold linking algebras are finite dimensional semisimple.
A pre-semisimple category is then
semisimple
if and only if it is Cauchy complete, i.e., it admits finite direct sums and all idempotents split.
The
Cauchy completion
of a linear category is the idempotent completion of the additive envelope.

Definition 2.6
.

A
unitary (1-)category
is a linear dagger category
{\mathcal{C}}
such that every
n
-fold linking algebra is a unitary algebra.
A unitary category is called
finite
if there is a global bound on the dimensions of the centers of all linking algebras.
That is, there is a
K>0
such that for any linking algebra
L=L(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})
,
\dim(Z(L))<K
.

Remark 2.7
.

The requirement that all the linking algebras be unitary algebras automatically means all unitary categories are
\mathrm{C}^{*}
and
\mathrm{W}^{*}
categories
[
GLR85
]
.
Moreover, a unitary category is semisimple if and only if it is Cauchy complete.
We note that a unitary category admits direct sums if and only if it admits orthogonal direct sums and is idempotent complete if and only if it is projection complete, i.e., all orthogonal projections split orthogonally.
We thus define the
Cauchy completion
of a unitary category as the projection completion of the orthogonal additive envelope.

Examples 2.8
.

The prototypical unitary category is
\mathsf{Hilb}
.
For any unitary algebra
A
, the
delooping

{\mathrm{B}}A
(the category with one object
\star
and
\End_{{\mathrm{B}}A}(\star)=A
) is a unitary category.
The
n
-fold linking algebras in
{\mathrm{B}}A
are canonically isomorphic to
M_{n}(A)
, and for any
M=(a_{i,j})\in M_{n}(A)
,
M^{*}=(a_{j,i}^{*})
.

Definition 2.9
.

A
(unitary) trace
on a unitary category
{\mathcal{C}}
is a collection of linear maps
\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{c}:\End_{\mathcal{C}}(c)\to{\mathbb{C}}
for each
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
such that:

(1)

\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{c}(gf)=\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{d}(fg)
for all
f:c\to d
and
g:d\to c
.

(2)

The sesquilinear form
\langle f|g\rangle_{c\to d}:=\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{c}(f^{\dagger}g)
on
{\mathcal{C}}(c\to d)
is positive definite.

A
pre-2-Hilbert space
is a finite unitary category equipped with a unitary trace.
Observe that the inner products
\langle f|g\rangle_{a\to b}
on the Hilbert spaces
{\mathcal{C}}(a\to b)
satisfy

(3)

\langle g|hf^{\dagger}\rangle_{b\to c}=\langle gf|h\rangle_{a\to c}=\langle f|g^{\dagger}h\rangle_{a\to b}\qquad\qquad\forall\,f:a\to b,\,g:b\to c,\,h:a\to c.

An
isometry
between two pre-2-Hilbert spaces is a fully faithful
{\dagger}
-functor which preserves the trace.

We call two pre-2-Hilbert spaces
isometrically equivalent
if there is an isometry
F\colon({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})\to({\mathcal{D}},\Tr^{\mathcal{D}})
which is also essentially surjective.
Note that this definition is equivalent to having isometries both ways together with unitary natural isomorphisms from their composites to the appropriate identity functors.

Examples 2.10
.

Given an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
(A,\Tr_{A})
, the unitary category
{\mathrm{B}}A
from Example
2.8
admits a canonical trace defined by the formula
\Tr^{{\mathrm{B}}A}_{\star}\big(\star\mathop{\longrightarrow}\limits^{a}\star\big):=\Tr_{A}(a)
. With this definition,
({\mathrm{B}}A,\Tr^{{\mathrm{B}}A})
is a pre-2-Hilbert space.

Definition 2.11

(cf.
[
Bae97
, Def 17]
)
.

We call a pre-2-Hilbert space
({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})
a
2-Hilbert space
if it is Cauchy complete, equivalently semisimple.
In this case, for
s\in{\mathcal{C}}
simple, we define its
quantum dimension

d_{s}:=\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}(\id_{s})
.

Definition 2.12
.

There is a 2-category
2\mathsf{Hilb}
whose objects are 2-Hilbert spaces. The 1-morphisms
{\mathcal{A}}\to{\mathcal{B}}
in
2\mathsf{Hilb}
are
{\dagger}
-functors, and the 2-morphisms are natural transformations.
This 2-category
2\mathsf{Hilb}
is a
{\dagger}
-2-category in the sense of
[
LR97
]

[
CHPJP22
, Def 2.2]
, with the dagger structure given by
(\eta^{\dagger})_{a}=(\eta_{a})^{\dagger}
.

We say two 2-Hilbert spaces are
isometrically equivalent
if they are isometrically equivalent as pre-2-Hilbert spaces.
Note that this notion of equivalence is stronger than the notion of equivalence in
2\mathsf{Hilb}
.
Indeed, it is straightforward to show that a
{\dagger}
-equivalence
F:({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})\to({\mathcal{D}},\Tr^{\mathcal{D}})
between two 2-Hilbert spaces is isometric if and only if it preserves quantum dimensions, i.e., for all
c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
,

d_{F(c)}=d_{c}
.

Example 2.13
.

If
({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})
is a pre-2-Hilbert space, then the Cauchy completion of
{\mathcal{C}}

is a 2-Hilbert space where if
\bigoplus c_{i}
is an orthogonal direct sum and
p\in\End(\bigoplus c_{i})
is an orthogonal projection, we define

\Tr_{(\bigoplus c_{i},p)}(f)=\Tr_{\bigoplus c_{i}}(pfp)=\Tr_{\bigoplus c_{i}}(f):=\sum_{i}\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{c_{i}}(p_{i}fp_{i}^{\dagger})\,,\qquad\forall\,f=pfp\in\End\left(\bigoplus c_{i}\right).

Example 2.14
.

Given an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
(A,\Tr_{A})
,
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}(A,\Tr_{A})
from Definition
2.3
is a 2-Hilbert space
which is isometrically equivalent, as a 2-Hilbert space, to the Cauchy completion of
({\mathrm{B}}A,\Tr^{{\mathrm{B}}A})
.

Moreover, every 2-Hilbert space is of this form.
Let
\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
denote a set of representatives for the simple objects of
{\mathcal{C}}
, and
set
X:=\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}c
.
Then
(A:=\End(X),\Tr_{A}:=\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{X})
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra such that
{\mathcal{C}}\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}(A,\Tr_{A})
isometrically.

Example 2.15
.

Suppose
({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})
is a 2-Hilbert space and
({\mathcal{D}},\Tr^{\mathcal{D}})
is a pre-2-Hilbert space.
Then
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}})
is again a pre-2-Hilbert space when equipped with the trace

\Tr_{F}(\rho:F\Rightarrow F)\coloneqq\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{D}}_{F(s)}(\rho_{s}).

Indeed, if
F,G:{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}
and
\rho:F\Rightarrow G
and
\sigma:G\Rightarrow F
, then

\displaystyle\Tr_{F}(\sigma\cdot\rho)

\displaystyle=\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{D}}_{F(s)}((\sigma\cdot\rho)_{s})=\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{D}}_{F(s)}(\sigma_{s}\circ\rho_{s})

\displaystyle=\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{D}}_{G(s)}(\rho_{s}\circ\sigma_{s})=\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{D}}_{G(s)}((\rho\cdot\sigma)_{s})=\Tr_{G}(\rho\cdot\sigma).

The scalars
d_{s}
are inserted into the formula above
for a unitary Yoneda result (
4
) below.
When
{\mathcal{D}}
is Cauchy complete, i.e. a 2-Hilbert space, so is
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}})
.

Remark 2.16
.

The equivalence
({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(\mathsf{Hilb}\to{\mathcal{A}})
given by
a\mapsto(H\mapsto H\otimes a)
is isometric for
({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})
a pre-2-Hilbert space.
Indeed, for
f\in{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a)
, by Example
2.15
, we have

\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(\mathsf{Hilb}\to{\mathcal{A}})}_{-\otimes a}(-\otimes f)=d_{{\mathbb{C}}}\cdot\Tr^{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{C}}\otimes a}({\mathbb{C}}\otimes f)=\Tr^{{\mathcal{A}}}_{a}(f).

We now quickly recall the unitary Yoneda results for 2-Hilbert spaces from
[
HPT24
, §2.1]
.
As noted in
[
GMP+23
, Rem. 3.61 and footnote]
, and implicitly used in
[
JP17
,
JP19
]
, a unitary trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}

and the associated inner products and their compatibility with
{\dagger}
in (
3
)
makes the Yoneda embedding

{\mathcal{C}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}^{\op}\to\mathsf{Hilb})\qquad\text{given by}\qquad c\mapsto{\mathcal{C}}(-\to c)

a dagger functor.
When
({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})
is a 2-Hilbert space and
\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
is a set of representatives of the simple objects of
{\mathcal{C}}
,
we have a canonical isometric equivalence

(4)

({\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{C}})\cong(\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}^{\op}\to\mathsf{Hilb}),\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}})

where for
F:{\mathcal{C}}^{\op}\to\mathsf{Hilb}
,

\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}}_{F}(\rho:F\Rightarrow F):=\sum_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}\cdot\Tr^{\mathsf{Hilb}}_{F(s)}(\rho_{s})

as in Example
2.15
.
We get a canonical unitary natural isomorphism

(5)

\upsilon_{c}:c\longmapsto\bigoplus_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}}(s\to c)\otimes s,

where the direct sum on the right hand side is the orthogonal direct sum.
The scalar
d_{s}^{-1}
indicates that the inner product on
{\mathcal{C}}(s\to c)
is scaled by
d_{s}^{-1}
, i.e.,

\langle f|g\rangle_{d_{s}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}}(s\to c)}=d_{s}^{-1}\langle f|g\rangle_{{\mathcal{C}}(s\to c)}=d_{s}^{-1}\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}(f^{\dagger}\circ g).

We call the elements of
d_{s}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}}(s\to c)
on the right hand side of (
5
) the
generalized elements
of
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
.

2.2.
Unitary dual functors, spherical weights, and unitary adjunction

We refer the reader to
[
JY21
]
for the basics of 2-category theory.
In this article, we make heavy use of the graphical calculus for 2-categories; we refer the reader to
[
HV19
, §8.1.2]
for the basics of the graphical calculus.
Our conventions are as follows:

•

We write 2-composition vertically from
bottom-to-top
.

•

We write 1-composition horizontally from
left-to-right
.

Definition 2.17
.

A
unitary adjoint functor
(UAF) for a rigid
{\dagger}
-2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}

is a choice of
\ev_{X},\coev_{X}
for every 1-morphism

Remark 2.18
.

Although all adjoint functors are canonically equivalent to each other in a contractible way, this equivalence need not be unitary.
Thus a UAF is structure, not property, as in
[
Pen20
]
.

Example 2.20
.

Recall that a
unitary multifusion category
is a multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
equipped with a dagger structure
{\dagger}
such that the coherence isomorphisms are all unitary.
We may view
{\mathcal{C}}
as a
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
with one object.
A UAF on
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
is exactly the notion of a unitary dual functor (UDF) on
{\mathcal{C}}
from
[
Pen20
]
.

By
[
Pen20
, Theorem A]
, UDFs on
{\mathcal{C}}
are classified by groupoid homomorphisms from the so-called
universal grading groupoid

{\mathcal{U}}_{\mathcal{C}}
of
{\mathcal{C}}
to
{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}
.
Since
{\mathbb{R}}_{>0}
has no torsion and
{\mathcal{U}}_{\mathcal{C}}
is finite, we see that

\Hom({\mathcal{U}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathbb{R}}_{>0})\cong\Hom({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathbb{R}}_{>0})

where
{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}
is the ‘matrix groupoid’ of
{\mathcal{C}}
which has one object for every
simple summand
1_{i}
of
1_{\mathcal{C}}
and a unique morphism from
1_{i}\to 1_{j}
whenever
1_{i}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\otimes 1_{j}\neq 0
.

Example 2.21

(
[
HPT24
, Def 2.2]
)
.

Suppose
{\mathcal{A}},{\mathcal{B}}\in 2\mathsf{Hilb}
and
F:{\mathcal{A}}\to{\mathcal{B}},\ G:{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{A}}
are functors.
We say that
F,G
are
unitary adjoints
, denoted

F\dashv^{\dagger}G
, if there is a family of natural unitary isomorphisms

{\mathcal{B}}(F(a)\to b)\cong{\mathcal{A}}(a\to G(b)).

Observe that this automatically implies that
F,G
are linear dagger functors, and we also have
G\dashv^{\dagger}F
.

exist and are unique up to unique unitary natural isomorphism.

,
G
is determined by unitary Yoneda (
4
) by

(6)

By
[
HPT24
, Prop 2.8]
, unitary adjunction is a UAF on
2\mathsf{Hilb}
.

.

.

), the unitary adjoint of

Example 2.24
.

Suppose
{\mathcal{C}}
is a unitary multifusion category.
By
[
Pen20
]
(see
[
HPT24
, Lem. 2.13]
),

•

If
{\mathcal{C}}
is indecomposable, each UDF on
{\mathcal{C}}
admits a unique spherical faithful state

\psi:{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}}\to 1_{\mathcal{C}})\to{\mathbb{C}}
normalized so that
\psi(\id_{1_{\mathcal{C}}})=1
.
Delooping,
\Psi_{\star}:=\psi
is a spherical weight on
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
.

•

When
{\mathcal{C}}
is arbitrary, for every faithful state
\psi
on
\End_{\mathcal{C}}(1_{{\mathcal{C}}})
, there is a unique UDF for which
\psi
is spherical.
Again, delooping, every choice of weight
\Psi_{\star}
on
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
admits a unique UAF for which
\Psi
is spherical.

2.3.
Semisimple 2-categories

Definition 2.25
.

Given a 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
and objects
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
, the
linking (
E_{1}
-)algebra

{\mathcal{L}}(a,b)
is the monoidal category

{\mathcal{L}}(a,b):=\begin{pmatrix}{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to a)&{\mathfrak{X}}(b\to a)\\
{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to b)&{\mathfrak{X}}(b\to b)\end{pmatrix}

where composition is component-wise, and tensor product is defined via a matrix multiplication formula.
Similarly, we can define the
n
-fold linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})
for every
a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\in{\mathcal{C}}
.

When
{\mathfrak{X}}
is
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
, so is every linking algebra with its obvious
{\dagger}
-transpose dagger structure.

Definition 2.26
.

A linear 2-category is called
pre-semisimple
if all
n
-fold linking algebras are semisimple multitensor categories.
A pre-semisimple 2-category is called
finite
if both

•

all
n
-fold linking algebras are multifusion, and

•

there is a global bound on the dimensions of
\End(1)
for the centers of all linking algebras.
That is, there is a
K>0
such that for any linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}={\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})
,
\dim(\End(1_{Z({\mathcal{L}})}))<K
.

Remark 2.27
.

Given a pre-semisimple
2
-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
,
we say
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
are
connected

when
{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to b)\neq 0
.
Since all 1-morphisms are dualizable and the 1-composite of non-zero 1-morphisms is non-zero,
connectedness is an equivalence relation.
The equivalence classes are called the
components
of
{\mathfrak{X}}
.

If
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
are in distinct components, then
the linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}={\mathcal{L}}(a,b)
splits as a direct sum
{\mathcal{L}}(a)\oplus{\mathcal{L}}(b)
, i.e., it is a decomposable multitensor category.
In turn, the center
Z({\mathcal{L}})
is decomposable as a braided multifusion category, and
the summands of
1_{Z({\mathcal{L}})}
correspond to the indecomposable fusion blocks of
{\mathcal{L}}
.

If
{\mathfrak{X}}
has
n
connected components, then we can choose representatives
\{a_{i}\}
of these components, and
{\mathcal{L}}={\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{n})
will decompose into
n
separate multifusion blocks.
It follows that
\dim\End(1_{Z({\mathcal{L}})})=n
.
In this way, the second condition on a finite pre-semisimple 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
can be interpreted as saying that
{\mathfrak{X}}
has no more than
K
components.

Finally, we note that the semisimple completion of a component is connected, and thus
K
is also an upper bound for the number of components of the semisimple completion of
{\mathfrak{X}}
.

Remark 2.28
.

There should be a natural coinductive generalization of (finite) pre-semsimple
n
-category for all
n
.
For example, a pre-semisimple
3
-category is a 3-category whose
n
-fold linking algebras are all semisimple 2-categories.
A pre-semisimple 3-category is finite if all
n
-fold linking algebras are finite semisimple 2-categories and there is a global bound on the dimensions of
\End_{Z({\mathcal{L}})}(\id_{1_{\mathcal{L}}})
for the centers of all linking algebras
{\mathcal{L}}
.

By
[
DR18
, §1.4.2]
, the (unital) condensation completion of the additive completion of a (finite) pre-semisimple 2-category is (finite) semisimple.
We now briefly recall these notions.
We begin with direct sums in 2-categories.

Definition 2.29
.

A direct sum of objects
a_{1},a_{2}
in a 2-category consists of an object
a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}
and 1-morphisms
I_{i}\colon a_{i}\to a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}
,
P_{i}\colon a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}\to a_{i}
for
i=1,2
such that

I_{i}\otimes P_{i}\cong 1_{a_{i}}\quad\text{and}\quad(P_{1}\otimes I_{1})\oplus(P_{2}\otimes I_{2})\cong 1_{a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}}.

We note that admitting these 2-isomorphisms is a property rather than structure; i.e. the space of choices of 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms satisfying these conditions is contractible.

Remark 2.30
.

By
[
DR18
, Prop 1.1.3]
, the 2-isomorphisms in Definition
2.29
can be chosen such that they witness the fact that
I_{c}
is both a left and right adjoint to
P_{c}
.

We now discuss (unital) condensation algebras in 2-categories.
We warn the reader that condensations in this article are always assumed to be unital.

Definition 2.31
.

An algebra
(A,\mu\colon A\otimes A\to A,\iota\colon 1\to A)
in a monoidal 1-category is said to be
separable Frobenius
if is equipped with an
A
-
A
bimodule map
\Delta:A\to A\otimes A
which splits
\mu
and
\Delta
admits a counit
\epsilon
.

A (unital)
condensation algebra

({}_{a}A_{a},\mu:A\otimes A\to A,\iota:1_{a}\to A)
in a 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a separable Frobenius algebra in the monoidal 1-category
\End_{{\mathfrak{X}}}(a)
.

Example 2.32
.

The monad associated to a separable adjunction is a condensation algebra.
In more detail,
given
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and an adjunction
{}_{a}X_{b}\dashv{}_{b}Y_{a}
, the monad associated to this adjunction is the algebra
({}_{a}X\otimes Y_{a},\mu=X\otimes\epsilon\otimes Y,\eta\colon 1_{a}\to X\otimes Y)
in
\End_{{\mathfrak{X}}}(a)
, where
\eta
and
\epsilon
are the unit and the counit of the adjunction.
The adjunction
{}_{a}X_{b}\dashv{}_{b}Y_{a}
is called
separable
if
\epsilon
admits a right inverse.

Definition 2.33
.

A
splitting
for a condensation algebra
A=({}_{a}A_{a},\mu:A\otimes A\to A,\iota:\id_{a}\to A)
is separable adjunction
{}_{a}X_{b}\dashv{}_{b}Y_{a}
whose associated monad is isomorphic to
A
as an algebra in
\End_{{\mathfrak{X}}}(a)
.
Whenever
X\dashv Y
is a splitting for
A
, we say

X\dashv Y

splits

A
, or simply that
A

splits
.

A 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
is said to be
condensation complete
if all condensation algebras split.

Definition 2.34

(
[
DR18
, Def 1.4.1]
)
.

A semisimple 2-category is a pre-semisimple 2-category which is additive and condensation complete.

Example 2.35
.

Suppose
{\mathcal{C}}
is a multifusion category.
The
delooping

{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
, which is the 2-category with one object
\star
whose endomorphisms is
{\mathcal{C}}
, is finite pre-semisimple.
The condensation completion of the additive completion of
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
is equivalent to the semisimple 2-category
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
.

Definition 2.36
.

The 3-category
3\mathsf{Vec}
has objects semisimple 2-categories, 1-morphisms linear 2-functors, 2-morphisms 2-natural transformations, and 3-morphisms modifications.
By
[
Déc22
]
,
the map
{\mathcal{C}}\mapsto\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
is an equivalence
\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Vec}
, where
\mathsf{mFC}
is the Morita 3-category of multifusion categories, with 1-morphisms bimodules categories, 2-morphisms bimodule functors, and 3-morphisms bimodule natural transformations.

3.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories and
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras

In this section, we endow a unitary multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
with the extra structure of a UDF and a spherical weight, which gives it a canonical structure of a 2-Hilbert space.
We call such a triple an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
Unitary module categories are also equipped with unitary module traces in the sense of
[
Sch13
,
GMP+23
]
to endow them with the structure of 2-Hilbert spaces.
We then define the notion of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra internal to
{\mathcal{C}}
, and we prove each module category equipped with a trace arises as
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
for an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
A\in{\mathcal{C}}
.
Here, we use unitary adjunction to endow the unitary internal hom with the structure of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra.
An essential point here is to choose the correct module trace on
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
for an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
and the correct UAF on the unitary 2-category
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras and their bimodules
so that:

•

the unitary internal end
[A,A]
is again unitarily isomorphic to
A
, and

•

the unitary adjoint of
-\otimes_{A}M_{B}:{\mathcal{C}}_{A}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{B}
is unitarily isomorphic to
-\otimes_{B}M^{\vee}_{A}
.

3.1.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories and their module categories

Definition 3.1
.

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
is a
triple
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
where

{\mathcal{C}}
is a unitary multifusion category,

\vee
is a UDF, and

\psi
is a spherical weight on
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
.

.

In fact, the data of an H*-multifusion category is precisely that of a unitary multifusion category
({\mathcal{C}},\vee)
equipped with a 2-Hilbert space structure such that

-\otimes c\dashv^{\dagger}-\otimes c^{\vee}\quad\text{and}\quad c\otimes-\dashv^{\dagger}c^{\vee}\otimes-\qquad\text{for all }c\in{\mathcal{C}}.

Notation 3.3
.

We write
1_{\mathcal{C}}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{k}1_{i}
for a decomposition into simples,
p_{i}
for the orthogonal projection onto
1_{i}
in
\End_{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}})

As usual, we write
d_{c}=\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}(\id_{c})
for
c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})

, and we abbreviate
d_{1_{i}}=:d_{i}
.
For
c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
, we write

s(c)=i
and
t(c)=j
for the unique
1\leq i,j\leq k
such that
c=1_{i}\otimes c\otimes 1_{j}
.
Observe that the coevaluation
1_{\mathcal{C}}\to c\otimes c^{\vee}
factors through
1_{s(c)}
and the evaluation
c^{\vee}\otimes c\to 1_{\mathcal{C}}
factors through
1_{t(c)}
.
This implies that

d_{s(c)}\dim_{L}^{\vee}(c)=(\psi\circ\tr_{L}^{\vee})(\id_{c})=d_{c}=(\psi\circ\tr_{R}^{\vee})(\id_{c})=d_{t(c)}\dim_{R}^{\vee}(c).

We now discuss module categories for
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories.
In this section, we discuss right modules, and we leave the notions for left modules to the reader.
We will, however, use left
{\mathcal{C}}
-modules frequently later in this article, and results proved for right
{\mathcal{C}}
-modules will also be used for left
{\mathcal{C}}
-modules without further comment.

Definition 3.4

(
[
Sch13
,
GMP+23
]
)
.

{\mathcal{C}}
be a unitary multifusion category equipped with a UDF
\vee

{\mathcal{C}}

{\mathcal{M}}

{\mathcal{M}}

c\in{\mathcal{C}}

Remark 3.5
.

The data of a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category
{\mathcal{M}}
equipped with a unitary module trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}
is precisely the data of a 2-Hilbert space
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}
-action on
{\mathcal{M}}
such that

-\triangleleft c\dashv_{\dagger}-\triangleleft c^{\vee}\qquad\forall c\in{\mathcal{C}}.

Definition 3.6
.

Given an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
,
the unitary 2-category
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
has:

•

objects are pairs
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
where
{\mathcal{M}}
is a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category and
\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}
is a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace

•

1-morphisms are unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functors, and

•

2-morphisms are natural transformations.

The next result is similar to results in
[
HPT24
, §2.3]
.

Lemma 3.7
.

Unitary adjunction on
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is a well-defined UAF.

Proof.

Under the 2-Hilbert space structure on a
{\mathcal{C}}
-module
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
, the functors
-\lhd c:{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{M}}
and
-\lhd c^{\vee}:{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{M}}
are unitary adjoints.
Given a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functor
F\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}}
, we can view the unitary modulator
\omega_{m,c}\colon F(m\lhd c)\to F(m)\lhd c
as a unitary crossing like a ‘half-brading’ for
F
with every
-\lhd c:{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{M}}
and
-\lhd c:{\mathcal{N}}\to{\mathcal{N}}

Unitarity of the map
\omega^{F^{*}}
follows as it is a
\pi
-rotation of a unitary under the UAF of unitary adjunction in
2\mathsf{Hilb}
.
The above definition automatically makes the unit and counit of the unitary adjunction
F\dashv^{\dagger}F^{*}
into
{\mathcal{C}}
-module natural transformations.
∎

We now list some general facts about module categories for
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories.

Facts 3.8
.

Suppose
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
is a unitary module for an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
.

(M1)

For every
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
,
-\lhd c:{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{M}}
is a unitary functor with unitary adjoint
-\lhd c^{\vee}
.

(M2)

For every
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
,
m\lhd-:{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}
is a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functor with unitary adjoint given by the unitary internal hom
[m,-]_{\mathcal{C}}\in{\mathcal{C}}
which is determined by (
6
):

{\mathcal{M}}(m\lhd c\to n)\cong{\mathcal{C}}(c\to[m,n]_{\mathcal{C}})\qquad\qquad[m,n]_{\mathcal{C}}:=\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{c}^{-1}{\mathcal{M}}(m\lhd c\to n)\otimes c.

(Note that
[m,-]_{\mathcal{C}}
is also a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functor by Lemma
3.7
above.)

Suppose
{\mathcal{C}}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category and
({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}),({\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{N}})
are unitary right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module categories.
Since
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
admits a forgetful functor to
2\mathsf{Hilb}
,

\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})}_{F}(\rho:F\Rightarrow F):=\sum_{m\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})}d_{m}\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}_{F(m)}(\rho_{m})

is a unitary trace on
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})
.
When
{\mathcal{M}}={\mathcal{C}}
, we would like that the map
n\mapsto n\lhd-
is an isometric equivalence

{\mathcal{N}}\to\mathsf{Fun}_{\mathcal{C}}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})
.
Unfortunately, the trace above is off by a scalar for each indecomposable summand of
{\mathcal{C}}
as we calculate below.

Suppose for simplicity that
{\mathcal{C}}
is indecomposable and let
1_{\mathcal{C}}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{d}1_{k}
be a decomposition into simples.
For
1\leq i,j\leq k
, define
{\mathcal{N}}_{i}:={\mathcal{N}}\lhd 1_{i}

and
{\mathcal{C}}_{ij}:=1_{i}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\otimes 1_{j}
.
Graphically, we represent
1_{i},1_{j}

\id_{n}
for

We now renormalize our initial guess for the trace on
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})
by this constant:

(8)

\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})}_{F}(\rho:F\Rightarrow F):=\frac{\dim(\End_{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}}))^{2}}{\operatorname{FPdim}({\mathcal{C}})\cdot\psi_{\mathcal{C}}(\id_{1_{\mathcal{C}}})}\cdot\sum_{m\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})}d_{m}\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}_{F(m)}(\rho_{m}).

With this renormalized trace, we have the following result.

Proposition 3.9
.

Suppose
{\mathcal{C}}
is an indecomposable
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category and
{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}}\in\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
.
The map
n\mapsto n\lhd-
is an isometric equivalence

{\mathcal{N}}\to\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})

when the latter is equipped with the unitary trace (
8
) in the case
{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}={\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}
.

3.2.
Bimodule categories and the relative Deligne product

For this section,
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
and
({\mathcal{D}},\vee,\psi)
are
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories.

Similar to a module category over an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category, a bimodule category must also be equipped with a bimodule trace.
In more detail, a bimodule trace for
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}
is a unitary trace on
{\mathcal{M}}
such that for all
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
,
d\in{\mathcal{D}}
,
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
, and
f:c\rhd m\lhd d\to c\rhd m\lhd d
,

As with module categories, the data of a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}
is precisely the same data as a 2-Hilbert space
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}-{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule action on
{\mathcal{M}}
such that

\displaystyle c\rhd-

\displaystyle\dashv^{\dagger}c^{\vee}\rhd-\qquad\forall c\in{\mathcal{C}},

\displaystyle-\lhd d

\displaystyle\dashv^{\dagger}-\lhd d^{\vee}\qquad\forall d\in{\mathcal{D}}.

Given a right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category
({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
and a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule category
({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}},\Tr^{\mathcal{N}})
, we can form the unitary Deligne product

{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
, which satisfies a universal property for
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced
{\dagger}
-functors
{\mathcal{M}}\times{\mathcal{N}}\to{\mathcal{P}}
for every unitary category
{\mathcal{P}}

[
ENO10
]
.
Similar to
[
ENO10
]
, there are several concrete models for the relative Deligne product; we look at two of them here.

•

The first is the category of left
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functors

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{{\mathcal{C}}}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})

with the trace from (
8
), which is manifestly a right
{\mathcal{D}}
-module trace.

•

The second is the unitary Cauchy completion of the
ladder category

[
BBJ19
]
whose objects are formal tensors
m\boxtimes n
for
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
and
n\in{\mathcal{N}}
and whose morphism spaces are given by

\Hom(m_{1}\boxtimes n_{1}\to m_{2}\boxtimes n_{2}):=\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}{\mathcal{M}}(m_{1}\to m_{2}\lhd c)\otimes{\mathcal{N}}(c\rhd n_{1}\to n_{2}).

Graphically, we represent simple tensors in a single summand of the above hom space by ‘ladders’:

Composition is given by ‘stacking ladders’ and decomposing using the fusion rules in
{\mathcal{C}}
.
The dagger is given by taking dagger in each tensorand in each summand and rotating the
{\mathcal{C}}
-strings using the UDF.
We refer the reader to
[
BBJ19
]
for more details.

The right
{\mathcal{D}}
-action here is given by

(m\boxtimes n)\lhd d:=m\boxtimes n\lhd d.

We equip the ladder category with a right
{\mathcal{D}}
-module trace in Lemma
3.11
below.

We prove these two models for the relative Deligne product are isometrically equivalent in Proposition
3.14
below.
For notational convenience, we will denote the unitary Cauchy completion of the ladder category by
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
and the functor category by
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})

To state the next lemma, we introduce the following notation.

Notation 3.10
.

We write
1_{\mathcal{C}}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{k}1_{i}
for a decomposition into simples.
We write
{\mathcal{M}}_{i}:={\mathcal{M}}\lhd 1_{i}
and
{\mathcal{N}}_{i}:=1_{i}\rhd{\mathcal{N}}
;
for
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
, we write
m_{i}:=m\lhd 1_{i}
and for
n\in{\mathcal{N}}
, we write
n_{i}:=1_{i}\rhd n
.

Lemma 3.11
.

The formula

\displaystyle\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}{\mathcal{M}}(m\to m\lhd c)\otimes{\mathcal{N}}(c\rhd n\to n)

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\bigoplus\delta_{c=1_{j}}}\bigoplus{\mathcal{M}}_{j}(m_{j}\to m_{j})\otimes{\mathcal{N}}_{i}(n_{j}\to n_{j})

\displaystyle\xrightarrow{\sum d_{j}^{-1}\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}}_{m_{j}}\otimes\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}_{n_{j}}}{\mathbb{C}}

defines a right
{\mathcal{D}}
-module trace on
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
.

Proof.

For a morphism

\sum_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}\sum_{r=1}^{k_{c}}f^{c}_{r}\otimes g^{c}_{r}\in\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}{\mathcal{M}}(m\to m^{\prime}\lhd c)\otimes{\mathcal{N}}(c\rhd n\to n^{\prime}),

we have

\displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j\\
b,c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}}_{ij})\\

∎

Corollary 3.12
.

The right
{\mathcal{C}}
-action map

{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}

is an isometric equivalence.

Proof.

This map is well known to be a unitary equivalence, so we show it is isometric.
To do so, it suffices to look at
m\boxtimes c
for
m\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})
and
c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
.
Consider a morphism

\sum_{d,r}f^{d}_{r}\otimes g^{d}_{r}:m\boxtimes c\to m\boxtimes c
,
where
f^{d}_{r}:m\to m\lhd d
and
g^{d}_{r}:d\otimes c\to c
with
d
ranging over
\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
.
By the formula in Lemma
3.11
, we have

\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{C}}}_{m\boxtimes c}(f)=\sum_{r}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}_{m}(f^{1_{s(c)}}_{r})\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}_{c}(g^{1_{s(c)}}_{r})d_{s(c)}^{-1}=\sum_{r}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}_{m}(f^{1_{s(c)}}_{r})(\psi\circ\tr^{\vee}_{L})(g^{1_{s(c)}}_{r})d_{s(c)}^{-1}.

On the other hand, the image of each
f^{d}_{r}\otimes g^{d}_{r}
under the action functor is
(\id_{m}\lhd g^{d}_{r})\circ(f^{d}_{r}\lhd\id_{c})
.
Denoting the image of
f
in
{\mathcal{M}}
by
\tilde{f}
, we have

\displaystyle\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}}_{m\lhd c}\left(\tilde{f}\right)

Now since
1_{s(c)}
is simple, a straightforward calculation shows that

\tr^{\vee}_{L}(g^{1_{s(c)}}_{i})=\frac{(\psi\circ\tr^{\vee}_{L})(g^{1_{s(c)}}_{i})}{d_{s(c)}}\id_{1_{s(c)}}.

The next corollary shows that every unitary module category over an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category admits a unitary module trace.
One should view this as the multifusion analog to the existence result
[
Sch13
]
for module traces for modules over a pseudounitary fusion category equipped with its canonical spherical structure.

Corollary 3.13
.

Suppose
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi_{\mathcal{C}})
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
If
{\mathcal{M}}
is a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module, then there exists a faithful
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace.
If
{\mathcal{C}}
and
{\mathcal{M}}
are indecomposable, this trace is unique up to positive scalar.

Proof.

We may assume
{\mathcal{C}}
and
{\mathcal{M}}
are indecomposable.
Since
{\mathcal{M}}
is indecomposable,
{\mathcal{M}}
is unitarily equivalent as a right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category to the unitary relative Deligne product
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}_{11}}{\mathcal{C}}
by
[
GMP+23
, Prop. 3.12]

where
{\mathcal{C}}_{11}:=1_{1}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\otimes 1_{1}
.
By
[
Sch13
,
GMP+23
]
, there is a unique faithful unitary right
{\mathcal{C}}_{11}
-module trace
\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}_{1}}
on
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}
up to positive scalar.
We also know
{\mathcal{C}}
admits a
{\mathcal{C}}_{11}
-
{\mathcal{C}}
bimodule trace given by
\psi\circ\tr_{L}^{\vee}=\psi\circ\tr_{R}^{\vee}
.
Hence applying Lemma
3.11
, we get a right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace on
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}_{11}}{\mathcal{C}}\cong{\mathcal{M}}
.
Finally, by indecomposability, there is at most one faithful unitary right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace
\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}}
on
{\mathcal{M}}
up to positive scalar.
∎

Now to identify
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
with
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{\mathcal{N}})
, we use
(M2)
.
Every
m^{\op}\in{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}
can be viewed as a functor
-\rhd m^{\op}:{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}
which has a unitary adjoint, and similarly for
n\in{\mathcal{N}}
.
Thus given
m\boxtimes n\in{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
, we get a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functor
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
by

(-\rhd n)\circ(-\rhd m^{\op})^{*}=\left(p^{\op}\mapsto\underbrace{[m^{\op},p^{\op}]_{\mathcal{C}}}_{=[p,m]_{\mathcal{C}}}\rhd n=\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{c}^{-1}\underbrace{{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}(c\rhd m^{\op}\to p^{\op})}_{={\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd c^{\vee})}\otimes c\rhd n\right).

We explain how this functor acts on a ‘simple tensor’ morphism
f\otimes g\in{\mathcal{M}}(m\lhd a\to m^{\prime})\otimes{\mathcal{N}}(n\to a\rhd n^{\prime})
for
a\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})
.
First, observe that morphisms of
[p,m]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n\to[p,m^{\prime}]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n^{\prime}
,
i.e., maps

\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{c}^{-1}\underbrace{{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}(c\rhd m^{\op}\to p^{\op})}_{={\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd c^{\vee})}\otimes c\rhd n\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{b\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{b}^{-1}\underbrace{{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}(b\rhd{m^{\prime}}^{\op}\to p^{\op})}_{={\mathcal{M}}(p\to m^{\prime}\lhd b^{\vee})}\otimes b\rhd n^{\prime},

can be viewed as block matrices of maps;
the
b,c
-block for
b,c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})

is a block of size

\dim({\mathcal{M}}(p\to m^{\prime}\lhd b^{\vee}))\times\dim({\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd c^{\vee}))

whose entries are morphisms
c\rhd n\to b\rhd n^{\prime}
.
We can think of the rows of this block as being indexed over an ONB
\{\gamma\}
for
d_{b}^{-1}{\mathcal{M}}(p\to m^{\prime}\lhd b^{\vee})
,
and the columns as being indexed over an ONB
\{\delta\}
for

d_{c}^{-1}{\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd c^{\vee})
.
The
b,c
-block of the morphism of
[p,m]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n\to[p,m^{\prime}]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n^{\prime}
corresponding to our simple tensor
f\otimes g
has

\gamma,\delta
-entry equal to

(9)

where the sum is independent of the choice of ONB for
{\mathcal{C}}(a\otimes c^{\vee}\to b^{\vee})

(which is isometrically isomorphic to
{\mathcal{C}}(b\otimes a\to c)
using
\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}=\psi\circ\tr_{L}
).
7
7

7

The meticulous reader may notice that the scalar
d_{b}^{-1}
from the inner product on
d_{b}^{-1}{\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd b^{\vee})

cancels with the normalization
\{\sqrt{d_{b}}\beta\}
needed to turn an ONB for
{\mathcal{C}}(a\otimes c^{\vee}\to b^{\vee})
with the inner product from
\Tr^{\mathcal{C}}
into an ONB for the closely related
isometry inner product
(e.g., see
[
JP20
, §2.5]
)
needed for functoriality.

We thus get a unitary
{\mathcal{D}}
-module functor

{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}\to\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})

by the universal property of Cauchy completion.
It is a straightforward but tedious exercise to prove this unitary functor is an equivalence; we leave the details to the interested reader.

Proposition 3.14
.

We have an isometric equivalence of unitary
{\mathcal{D}}
-modules

{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{\mathcal{N}})

where the latter has the trace from (
8
).

Proof.

It remains to to prove the above unitary equivalence is isometric.
It is enough to show that it is trace-preserving for endomorphisms of objects of the form
m\boxtimes n
, since all objects are direct sums of summands of objects in this form.
We can assume
m,n
are simple with
s(m)=t(n)=1_{i}
.
Let

(f:m\to m\lhd a)\otimes(g:a\rhd n\to n)\in\bigoplus_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}{\mathcal{M}}(m\to m\lhd c)\otimes{\mathcal{N}}(c\rhd n\to n)

be a ‘simple tensor’ morphism in the ladder category.
Note we must have
a\in{\mathcal{C}}_{i}
for this to be nonzero.
By the formula in Lemma
3.11
, we have

\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}}_{m\boxtimes n}(f\otimes g)=\sum_{i}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}(f^{1_{t(a)}}_{i})\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}(g^{1_{t(a)}}_{i})d_{t(a)}^{-1}=\delta_{a=1_{i}}d_{1_{i}}^{-1}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}(f)\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}(g).

On the other hand, we can compute the trace in

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})
of
the block matrix associated to our ‘simple tensor’ morphism
f\otimes g
.
Clearly the trace only sees entries in the block diagonal of this matrix corresponding to the blocks where
b=c
.
Analyzing (
9
),
since
\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}
is a left
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace, the trace of the image of
f\otimes g
will only be non-zero if
a=1_{i}
;
the reasoning here is similar to that used in the proof of Corollary
3.12
.
In this case, since
m,n
were assumed simple,
f,g
are scalars, so it suffices to consider the case
f=\id_{m}
and
g=\id_{n}
.
By the formula in (
8
), we have

\displaystyle\Tr^{\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})}_{(-\rhd n)\circ(-\rhd m^{\op})^{*}}(\id)

\displaystyle=\frac{d_{1_{i}}}{\dim({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}\sum_{p\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})}d_{p}\Tr^{{\mathcal{N}}}_{[p,m]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n}(\id_{[p,m]_{\mathcal{C}}\rhd n})

\displaystyle=\frac{d_{1_{i}}}{\dim({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}\sum_{p\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})}d_{p}\sum_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}\dim({\mathcal{M}}(p\to m\lhd c^{\vee}))\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}_{c\rhd n}(\id_{c\rhd n})

\displaystyle=\frac{d_{1_{i}}}{\dim({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}\sum_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}_{m\lhd c^{\vee}}(\id_{m\lhd c^{\vee}})\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}_{c\rhd n}(\id_{c\rhd n})

\displaystyle\underset{\text{\eqref{eq:PopBubbles}}}{=}\frac{d_{1_{i}}}{\dim({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}\sum_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}}_{i})}d_{m}\frac{d_{c}}{d_{1_{i}}}d_{n}\frac{d_{c}}{d_{1_{i}}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{d_{1_{i}}}d_{m}d_{n}

\displaystyle=\Tr^{{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}}_{m\boxtimes n}(\id_{m\boxtimes n}).

The result follows.
∎

In what follows, we briefly describe the universal property that
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}}{\mathcal{N}}
enjoys.

Definition 3.15
.

For a left
{\mathcal{C}}
-module
{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{C}}}
and right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module
{}_{{\mathcal{C}}}{\mathcal{N}}
, a
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced
{\dagger}
-functor into a 2-Hilbert space
{\mathcal{P}}
consists of a functor

satisfying the obvious associativity and unitality axioms.
A
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced natural transformation
\eta\colon F\Rightarrow G
between
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced functors is a natural transformation between the underlying functors which intertwines the actions of the unitary constraints
F^{\alpha}
and
G^{\alpha}
.
We denote the unitary category of
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced functors and
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced natural transformations by
\mathsf{Bal}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}};{\mathcal{P}})
.

It is easy to see that
\mathsf{Bal}
is functorial in
{\mathcal{M}}
,
{\mathcal{N}}
, and
{\mathcal{P}}
.

Remark 3.16
.

There exists a universal
{\mathcal{C}}
-balanced functor

\iota\in\mathsf{Bal}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}};{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})

such that for every 2-Hilbert space
{\mathcal{P}}
, precomposition with
\iota
is an equivalence of unitary categories

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}\to{\mathcal{P}})\xrightarrow{\iota^{*}}\mathsf{Bal}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}};{\mathcal{P}}).

We note that this universal property only determines
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
up to unitary equivalence.
Once a unitary 2-categorical Yoneda lemma has been established, we expect that
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}
can be determined up to isometric equivalence as the object representing the functor

\mathsf{Bal}_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}};-)\colon 2\mathsf{Hilb}\to 2\mathsf{Hilb}.

Remark 3.17
.

For H*-multifusion categories
{\mathcal{C}}
and
{\mathcal{D}}
,
one may easily generalize the notion of a balanced functor from a left
{\mathcal{C}}
-module
{\mathcal{M}}
, a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule
{\mathcal{N}}
, and a right
{\mathcal{D}}
-module
{\mathcal{O}}
.
For a 2-Hilbert space
{\mathcal{P}}
, this yields a unitary category

\mathsf{Bal}_{{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}},{\mathcal{O}};{\mathcal{P}}).

It is then easy to show that both
{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{N}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{D}}{\mathcal{O}})
and
({\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})\boxtimes_{\mathcal{D}}{\mathcal{O}}
represent the functor
\mathsf{Bal}_{{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}}({\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}},{\mathcal{O}};-)
. This provides a unitary associativity constraint, which we conjecture to be isometric.

In general, one can define balanced functors for arbitrarily many bimodules, which will provide unitary higher associativity constraints.

3.3.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras

For this section,
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
We now generalize the notion of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra to a
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-Frobenius algebra which is separable (multiplication splits as a bimodule map) and standard (a compatiblity condition with
\vee
).
The similar notion of special standard Q-system or standard separable
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-Frobenius algebra (SSFA) was studied in

[
CHPJP22
]
and
[
Ver22
, §3.1]
.
In both of those articles, the separator was required to be the adjoint of multiplication.
Moreover, in the former article, duality was completely ignored, and in the latter article, only the standard spherical UAF was analyzed.
To distinguish the setting we study here, we will call our objects of study
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras.
(Notice also the notion of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra agrees exactly with that of a standard Q-system from
[
BKLR15
]
, so we avoid using the term ‘Q-system’ here to avoid confusion.)

Definition 3.18
.

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
algebra
in a

{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)

consists of an (associative, unital) algebra
(A,\mu,\iota)
which satisfies certain axioms.
We represent
A
,
\mu
,
\iota
and their adjoints
\mu^{\dagger}
,
\iota^{\dagger}
graphically as follows:

{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra is called a

or

{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-Frobenius algebra
if

Facts 3.19
.

We now list some basic facts about
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras.

(A1)

The
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in
\mathsf{Hilb}
equipped with its standard UDF and trace
\Tr_{H}^{{\mathrm{B}}\mathsf{Hilb}}:=\Tr_{B(H)}

{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in the sense of Definition
2.2

First, by the GNS construction,
every such
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
(A,\Tr_{A})
gives a Hilbert space

which is
A
again with inner product

\langle a|b\rangle_{L^{2}(A,\Tr_{A})}:=\Tr(a^{*}b).

It is straightforward to verify that
L^{2}(A,\Tr_{A})
with its multiplication and unit is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra.

(A2)

Every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra is (non-unitarily) equivalent to a standard Q-system.
Indeed, for
\rm H^{*}
-algebra
(A,\mu,\iota)
,
setting
x:=(\mu\mu^{\dagger})^{\frac{1}{2}}
,
(A,x^{-1}\mu,x\iota)
is a standard Q-system,
where the equivalence is given by
x
.

(A3)

By combining
(A2)
and
[
CHPJP22
, Facts 3.4]
,

•

{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-Frobenius follows automatically from unitality, associativity, and separability.

•

Associativity follows automatically from
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-Frobenius and separable.

(A4)

Given an algebra
A
satisfying
(

H
enumi

1)
, then
(

H
enumi

2)
is equivalent to ordinary separability.
Indeed,
(

H
enumi

1)
implies that the category of
A
-
A
bimodules
{}_{A}{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is unitary and semisimple, and thus equivalent to
\mathsf{Hilb}^{\oplus n}
for some finite
n
.
In
\mathsf{Hilb}^{\oplus n}
, a morphism
f:x\to y
is right invertible if and only if
ff^{\dagger}
is invertible.

The standardness condition

H

Observe that the above morphisms are unitary if and only if they are equal; the dagger of the first map is the inverse of the second.
It follows immediately that
(

H
enumi

3)
implies that without loss of generality, the evaluation and coevaluation morphisms for
A
assigned by the UDF are given by
\ev_{A}=\iota^{\dagger}\circ\mu
and
\coev_{A}=\mu^{\dagger}\circ\iota
.

Example 3.20
.

Suppose
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
,
and recall that
\id_{c}\otimes\ev_{c}\ev_{c}^{\dagger}\otimes\id_{c^{\vee}}
is invertible in
\End(c\otimes c^{\vee})
by
[
Zit07
, Cor. 1.19]
, see also
[
CHPJP22
, Facts 3.5(Z3)]
.
Then

c\otimes c^{\vee}
has a canonical structure of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
with multiplication and unit given by

\mu:=\id_{c}\otimes\ev_{c}\otimes\id_{c^{\vee}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\iota:=\coev_{c}.

The only interesting thing to verify is
(

H
enumi

3)
, which follows as
\vee
is a UDF.
Indeed,
c\otimes c^{\vee}
is canonically symmetrically self-dual, so identifying
(c\otimes c^{\vee})^{\vee}\cong c\otimes c^{\vee}
,
the morphisms in the equivalent condition listed under
(

H
enumi

3)
are both identities.
(Here, we use that
\coev_{c^{\vee}}=\ev^{\dagger}_{c}
and
\ev_{c^{\vee}}=\coev_{c}^{\dagger}
.)

A particular case of the above example gives a more conceptual approach to the construction in
[
NY18
, Appendix A]
that the internal endomorphisms of any object in unitary module category for a unitary tensor category can be equipped with the structure of a Q-system.

Sub-Example 3.21
.

Given a right unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category
{\mathcal{M}}
equipped with a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}
,
we get a ‘linking’ unitary multifusion category

{\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{C}}})\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}{\mathcal{C}}&{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}\\
{\mathcal{M}}&\End({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})\end{pmatrix}.

The tensor products in this category are given by

\begin{pmatrix}0&n^{\op}\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}\otimes\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
m&0\end{pmatrix}:=\begin{pmatrix}[n,m]&0\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
m&0\end{pmatrix}\otimes\begin{pmatrix}0&n^{\op}\\
0&0\end{pmatrix}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\
0&m\lhd[n,-]\end{pmatrix}

where the internal hom
[n,m]
is taken under the unitary adjunction

{\mathcal{M}}(n\lhd c\to m)\cong{\mathcal{C}}(c\to[n,m]),

i.e.,
[n,-]
is the unitary adjoint of
n\lhd-
.
Observe that
{\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})
is equivalent to the unitary multifusion category

\End_{\mathcal{C}}({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\boxplus{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{C}}})=\begin{pmatrix}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})&\Hom({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})\\
\Hom({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})&\End({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})\end{pmatrix},

where

m\in{\mathcal{M}}
corresponds to
m\lhd-\in\Hom({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})

and

n^{\op}\in{\mathcal{M}}^{\op}
corresponds to
[n,-]\in\Hom({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})
.
Unitary adjunction gives a canonical UDF on this unitary multifusion category such that the inclusion
{\mathcal{C}}\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{L}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}})
is unitary pivotal.
Unpacking,
the dual for
m
is
m^{\op}
.
The evaluation map
\ev_{m}:m\otimes m^{\op}\Rightarrow\id_{\mathcal{M}}
is the mate of the identity natural transformation under the unitary adjunction

{\mathcal{M}}(m\lhd[m,-]\to-)\cong{\mathcal{C}}([m,-]\to[m,-]).

The map
\coev_{m}:1_{\mathcal{C}}\to m^{\op}\otimes m
is given by the mate of
\id_{m}
under the unitary adjunction

{\mathcal{M}}(m,m)\cong{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}},[m,m]).

Note that the conventions for duals are opposite to our usual conventions as composition of functors is read right-to-left, which is opposite the left-to-right convention for usual tensor products.

We conclude that by the above Example
3.20
, for any
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
, the unitary internal end
\underline{\End}_{\mathcal{C}}(m)=[m,m]=m^{\op}\otimes m
has a canonical
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra structure.

Definition 3.22
.

The
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in
{\mathcal{C}}
are the objects in a unitary 2-category
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
whose 1-morphisms are unital, associative bimodules and whose 2-morphisms are intertwiners.
The structure of this 2-category is closely related to the
Q-system completion

\mathsf{QSys}({\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}})
studied in
[
CHPJP22
]
and the category
\mathsf{Bimod}({\mathcal{C}})
studied in
[
Ver22
]
; the main difference is that we must now correct for the bubble term
\mu\mu^{\dagger}
which no longer pops.
We explain where these differences occur below.

A
bimodule
for two
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras
A,B
in
{\mathcal{C}}
is an object
M\in{\mathcal{C}}
together with maps
\lambda:A\otimes M\to M
and
\rho:M\otimes B\to M
which are unital and associative.
As above, we represent
\lambda,\rho
by trivalent vertices whose vertical reflections are their adjoints.

Given an
A
-
B
bimodule
M
, its dual
M^{\vee}
carries a
B
-
A
bimodule structure given on the right hand side in the diagram below.
Since
M
is separable as both a left and right module,

\ev_{M}^{\mathcal{C}}:M^{\vee}\otimes M\to 1_{\mathcal{C}}

and

\coev_{M}^{\mathcal{C}}:1_{\mathcal{C}}\to M\otimes M^{\vee}

both absorb the corresponding separability idemopotents, as in the right hand side of the diagrams below.

which all yield the identical coherence isomorphisms
\nu:a^{\vee}\otimes b^{\vee}\to(b\otimes a)^{\vee}
and
\varphi:a\to a^{\vee\vee}
.
Moreover, for each of these UAFs on
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
, the organic inclusion
{\mathcal{C}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
by
1_{\mathcal{C}}\mapsto 1_{\mathcal{C}}
is unitary pivotal.

Remark 3.23
.

It was posited in
[
CHPJP22
]
that the unitary version of a condensation
monad in the spirit of
[
GJF19
]
in a
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-category is a not necessarily unital special Q-system.
It was pointed out to us by David Reutter that if we require a not necessarily unital special Q-system to be compatible with the ambient UDF in an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category

(11)

so that any morphism between 1-composite powers of
A
’s only depends on the connectivity of the graph, then
A
is automatically unital.
Indeed, using
(

H
enumi

1)
and capping off (
11
), one shows
A
has both a right and a left unit given by

\scriptstyle A^{\vee}

and

\scriptstyle A^{\vee}

respectively,
and thus they are automatically equal.
The above can also be adjusted for
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras by including factors of the bubble inverse.
This fact justifies working solely with unital algebras.

defines a unitary operator-valued

{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace

\tau_{M}:{\mathcal{C}}_{A}(M\to M)\to\End({}_{A}A_{A})
, which takes values in an abelian unitary algebra.
Post-composing with any faithful weight
\phi:\End({}_{A}A_{A})\to{\mathbb{C}}
yields a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace on
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
.
By Corollary
3.13
, every unitary module trace on
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is of this form, as the indecomposable summands of
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
correspond to the simple algebra summands of
A
.

We now determine the faithful weight
\phi:\End({}_{A}A_{A})\to{\mathbb{C}}
(up to uniform scalar) such that the unitary internal hom
[A,A]
is unitarily isomorphic to
A
.

A\in{\mathcal{C}}

Proposition 3.25
.

f,g
are right
A
-module maps and

By (
5
), we have canonical unitary isomorphisms

A\cong\bigoplus_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}}(s\to A)\otimes s\qquad\text{and}\qquad[A,A]_{\mathcal{C}}\cong\bigoplus_{s\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}})}d_{s}^{-1}{\mathcal{C}}_{A}(s\otimes A\to A)\otimes s,

where the second isomorphism implicitly uses the unitary adjunction
{\mathcal{C}}(s\to[A,A]_{\mathcal{C}})\cong{\mathcal{C}}_{A}(s\otimes A\to A)
.

Corollary 3.26
.

N\boxtimes_{A}M^{\vee}

We now combine the above results into the main result of this subsection.

Theorem 3.28
.

A unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category equipped with a unitary trace

({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
is isometrically equivalent to
({\mathcal{C}}_{A},\Tr^{{\mathcal{C}}_{A}})
where
A=[m,m]_{\mathcal{C}}
for any generator
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
.
Hence every
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
comes from an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra.

Proof.

We first recall the construction of the unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module equivalence
{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
.
We first define it on the full subcategory
{\mathcal{M}}_{0}\subset{\mathcal{M}}
whose objects are of the form
c\rhd m
for
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
.
We then extend it to an equivalence
{\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
by the universal property of Cauchy completion.
The functor
{\mathcal{M}}_{0}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is given on objects by
c\rhd m\mapsto c\otimes A
and on morphisms by

3.5.
Equivalence of unitary 2-categories
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})

By Theorem
3.28
, we have a unitary equivalence of unitary 2-categories
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
given by

•

A\mapsto{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
,

•

{}_{A}M_{B}\mapsto-\boxtimes_{A}M_{B}
, and

•

(f:{}_{A}M_{B}\Rightarrow{}_{A}N_{B})\mapsto-\boxtimes_{A}f
.

We saw in Lemma
3.7
above that
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is equipped with a canonical UAF given by unitary adjunction, and in (
10
) above, we found a 1-parameter family of UAFs on
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
.
We now choose the correct UAF on
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
making this unitary equivalence preserve the UAFs, i.e., the unitary adjoint of
-\boxtimes_{A}M_{B}
is
-\boxtimes_{B}M^{\vee}_{A}
.

Proposition 3.29
.

The choice
\delta=0
from (
10
)
for the UAF on
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})

make the functors
-\boxtimes_{A}M_{B}:{\mathcal{C}}_{A}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{B}
and
-\boxtimes_{B}M_{A}^{\vee}:{\mathcal{C}}_{B}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
unitary adjoints.
Hence the unitary equivalence
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is compatible with UAFs and thus unitary pivotal.

Proof.

The isomorphism
{\mathcal{C}}_{B}(N_{A}\boxtimes_{A}M_{B}\to P_{B})\cong{\mathcal{C}}_{A}(N_{A}\to P_{B}\boxtimes_{B}M_{A}^{\vee})

4.
3-Hilbert spaces

Now that we have completed our analysis of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories and their modules, we turn our attention to the notion of a 3-Hilbert space.
We begin with pre-3-Hilbert space, with the basic example begin an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
We then discuss Hilbert direct sums and
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monads, together with their corresponding completion operations.
Finally, 3-Hilbert spaces are introduced as ‘completed’ pre-3-Hilbert spaces, and we show they are all of the form
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\cong\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
for an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.

4.1.
pre-3-Hilbert spaces

Definition 4.1
.

A
unitary 2-category
is a
{\dagger}
-2-category such that every
n
-fold linking algebra from Definition
2.25
with its obvious dagger structure is a unitary multitensor category.
Thus unitary 2-categories are pre-semisimple.
A unitary 2-category is called
finite
if it is finite as a pre-semisimple 2-category.

Example 4.2
.

For a unitary multitensor category
{\mathcal{C}}
,
the 2-category of semisimple unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module categories, dualizable unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functors, and uniformly bounded
{\mathcal{C}}
-module natural transformations is a unitary 2-category.
When
{\mathcal{C}}
is unitary multifusion, the 2-category
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
of finite semsimple unitary module categories is a finite unitary 2-category.

Definition 4.3
.

A
pre-3-Hilbert space

({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
is a finite unitary 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
equipped with a UAF
\vee
and a spherical tracial weight
\Psi
on
\End(1_{a})
for all objects
a\in{\mathfrak{X}}
.

Notice that given a pre-3-Hilbert space
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
, we may uniformly rescale the spherical weight
\Psi
on each component of
{\mathfrak{X}}
independently to obtain a new pre-3-Hilbert space.

Example 4.4
.

The basic example of a pre-3-Hilbert space is
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
where
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.

Example 4.5
.

Given any pre-3-Hilbert space
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
,
for every
a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
,
the linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})
has an
organic structure of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category with UDF induced by the UAF of
{\mathfrak{X}}

and
spherical weight
\psi
induced by the spherical weight
\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}}
.

Remark 4.6
.

A pre-3-Hilbert space structure on
{\mathfrak{X}}
induces a 2-Hilbert space structure on each hom-category
{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to b)
.
Indeed, for
X\in{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to b)
, we define
\Tr_{X}\colon\End(X)\to{\mathbb{C}}
by

Example 4.7
.

Let
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
be an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category, and recall from Lemma
3.7
that unitary adjunction is a UAF on
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
.
We claim that defining

\Psi_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}(\eta)\coloneqq\sum_{m\in\Irr({\mathcal{M}})}d_{m}\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}_{m}(\eta_{m})

for
{\mathcal{C}}
-module natural transformations
\eta:\id_{\mathcal{M}}\Rightarrow\id_{\mathcal{M}}
defines a spherical weight on
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
endowing it with the structure of a pre-3-Hilbert space.

{\mathcal{C}}
-module functor

Note, however, that under this choice of spherical weight, the induced 2-Hilbert space structure on
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}({}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}})
does not agree with the 2-Hilbert space structure from (
8
).
We thus
renormalize

\Psi^{\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}
on each component so that these 2-Hilbert space structures agree.
In explicit detail, suppose

{\mathcal{C}}=\boxplus{\mathcal{C}}_{j}
is a decomposition of
{\mathcal{C}}
into indecomposable summands.
Then
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})=\boxplus\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}_{j})
is a decomposition into components.
We rescale
\Psi^{\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}
on the
j
-th component by multiplying by the scalar

\frac{\dim(\End_{{\mathcal{C}}_{j}}(1_{{\mathcal{C}}_{j}}))^{2}}{\operatorname{FPdim}({\mathcal{C}}_{j})\cdot\psi_{\mathcal{C}}(\id_{1_{{\mathcal{C}}_{j}}})}

which appeared in (
8
) above.

Sub-Example 4.8
.

Choosing
{\mathcal{C}}=\mathsf{Hilb}
in the above example with its canonical UDF and trace, we see that
2\mathsf{Hilb}
is a pre-3-Hilbert space with

\Psi_{\mathcal{A}}(\eta:\id_{\mathcal{A}}\Rightarrow\id_{\mathcal{A}}):=\sum_{a\in\Irr({\mathcal{A}})}d_{a}\Tr^{\mathcal{A}}_{a}(\eta_{a}).

Observe that no renormalization is necessary for the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
\mathsf{Hilb}
equipped with its canonical spherical state normalized so that
\psi(\id_{\mathbb{C}})=1
.

Note that in the first and last equations, we used traciality of pivotal trace associated to
(X^{*},\ev^{*}_{X},\coev_{X}^{*})
.
By non-degeneracy of
\Psi
, we see that
\zeta^{\dagger}_{X}\zeta_{X}=\zeta^{-1}_{X}(\zeta^{\dagger}_{X})^{-1}
.
But since
\zeta^{\dagger}_{X}\zeta_{X}
is positive, the only way it can equal its own inverse is if it equals
\id_{X^{*}}
.
We conclude that
\zeta_{X}
is unitary.
∎

4.2.
Isometries, coisometries, and Hilbert direct sums

In a unitary 2-category, it makes sense to talk about orthogonal direct sums.
Given
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
, their
orthogonal direct sum
is a direct sum
a\boxplus b
such that the isomorphisms
I_{c}\otimes P_{c}\cong 1_{c}
are unitary for
c=a,b
,
and the isomorphism

(P_{a}\otimes I_{a})\oplus(P_{b}\otimes I_{b})\cong 1_{a\boxplus b}

is both unitary and witnesses
1_{a\boxplus b}
as an orthogonal direct sum.

As in Remark
2.30
, we may sill arrange that
I_{c}
is both left and right adjoint to
P_{c}
for
c=a,b
while keeping the desired direct sum orthogonal.
However, when working in a pre-3-Hilbert space, these adjunctions need not be compatible with the ambient UAF (see Remark
4.19
below).
Thus the notion of orthogonal direct sum is not sufficient for the purposes of this article.

Definition 4.10
.

Suppose
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
is a pre-3-Hilbert space and
a,b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
.
A 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}
is called an
isometry
if
\coev_{X}:1_{a}\to{}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}

is unitary
and

\ev_{X}:{}_{b}X^{\vee}\otimes_{a}X_{b}\to 1_{b}
is an isometry.

a,b,{}_{a}X_{b},{}_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}

A 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}
is called a
co-isometry
if
{}_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}
is an isometry, i.e.,

\ev_{X}:{}_{b}X^{\vee}\otimes_{a}X_{b}\to 1_{b}
is unitary
and

\coev_{X}:1_{a}\to{}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}

is a coisometry.
Graphically, the relations for a co-isometry are

An
isometric equivalence
is a 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}
that is both an isometry and a co-isometry, i.e., an adjoint equivalence with respect to our UAF
\vee
.

Remark 4.11
.

A coisometry is stronger than the notion of a dagger condensation in the sense of
[
CP22
]
; see also
[
GJF19
]
.

Remark 4.12
.

is an isometry (resp. co-isometry) if and only if
