Example 4.13
.

We show that the isometries in
2\mathsf{Hilb}
are the fully faithful
\Tr
-preserving
{\dagger}
-functors.
Thus the two notions of isometry for unitary functors between two 2-Hilbert spaces from Definitions
2.9
and
4.10
agree.

Suppose
F:({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})\to({\mathcal{B}},\Tr^{\mathcal{B}})
is a unitary functor.
When
F
is fully faithful, then
F
maps distinct simples in
{\mathcal{A}}
to distinct simples in
{\mathcal{B}}
.
Moreover,
F^{*}:{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{A}}
is the projection map onto the image of
{\mathcal{A}}
, i.e., if
b\in\Irr({\mathcal{B}})
, then
F^{*}(b)=a\in\Irr({\mathcal{A}})
if
F(a)=b
, and otherwise
F^{*}(b)=0
.
Since
F\dashv^{\dagger}F^{*}
, we have a unitary isomorphism

{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a)={\mathcal{A}}(F^{*}F(a)\to a)\cong{\mathcal{B}}(F(a)\to F(a)),

and since
(\coev_{F})_{a}=\mate(\id_{F(a)})
, we see that
(\coev_{F})_{a}=\lambda_{a}\id_{a}

for some
\lambda_{a}\in{\mathbb{C}}^{\times}
which is unimodular if and only if
d_{F(a)}=d_{a}
.
We conclude that when
F
is fully faithful,
\coev_{F}
is unitary if and only if
F
is trace-preserving.
It follows by a similar calculation or by (
17
) that
\ev_{F}
is an isometry.

Conversely, if
F
is an isometry, then
\coev_{F}:\id_{\mathcal{A}}\Rightarrow F^{*}\circ F
is unitary and thus invertible, so
F
is fully faithful.
The above argument then applies to show that
F
is trace preserving.

Definition 4.14
.

Given two pre-3-Hilbert spaces
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee_{\mathfrak{X}},\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}})
and
({\mathfrak{Y}},\vee_{\mathfrak{Y}},\Psi^{\mathfrak{Y}})
,
we write
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger}}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
for the unitary 2-category of unitary 2-functors
{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
.

We say a unitary 2-functor
F:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
is
UAF-preserving
if for every 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}\in{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to b)
, the canonical isomorphism

\scriptstyle F(X^{\vee})
\scriptstyle F(X)
\scriptstyle F(X)^{\vee}
F^{2}_{X^{\vee},X}
F(\ev_{X})
\coev_{F(X)}

is unitary.
We write

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})

for the full unitary 2-subcategory of
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger}}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
of UAF-preserving unitary 2-functors.

We say a
{\dagger}
2-functor
F:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
is an
isometry

if

\Psi^{\mathfrak{Y}}_{F(a)}(F(f))=\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}}_{a}(f)\qquad\qquad\forall\,f\in\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(1_{a}),\,\,\forall\,a\in{\mathfrak{X}}.

We write
\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
for the full unitary 2-subcategory of
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
whose objects are isometries.
By Proposition
4.9
,
\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
is a full unitary 2-subcategory of
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.

We say two pre-3-Hilbert spaces are
isometrically equivalent
if there is an isometric
{\dagger}
-equivalence
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee_{\mathfrak{X}},\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}})\to({\mathfrak{Y}},\vee_{\mathfrak{Y}},\Psi^{\mathfrak{Y}})
which is
isometrically essentially surjective
, i.e., for every
b\in{\mathfrak{Y}}
, there is an
a\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and an isometric equivalence
{}_{F(a)}Y_{b}
.
Note that the notion of isometric equivalence is strictly stronger than
{\dagger}
-equivalence of the underlying unitary 2-categories.

Remark 4.15
.

We conjecture there is a canonical pre-3-Hilbert structure on
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
such that the following are equivalent:

(1)

F\in\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
is an isometric equivalence between pre-3-Hilbert spaces;

(2)

There exist isometric equivalences
\eta\colon F^{*}F\Rightarrow\id_{\mathfrak{X}}
in
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{X}})
and
\epsilon\colon\id_{\mathfrak{Y}}\Rightarrow FF^{*}
in
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{Y}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
, where
F^{*}
is the unitary adjoint of
F
.

Example 4.16
.

Given
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
and
({\mathcal{D}},\vee,\psi)
, and a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}
, there is a
{\dagger}
-2-functor

-\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}\colon\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})

Definition 4.17
.

A
Hilbert direct sum
of objects
a_{1},a_{2}
in a pre-3-Hilbert space consists of an object
a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}
and isometries

I_{j}\colon a_{j}\to a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}

for
j=1,2

such that

\ev_{1}\ev_{1}^{\dagger}+\ev_{2}\ev_{2}^{\dagger}=\id_{1_{a_{1}\boxplus a_{2}}}
where
\ev_{j}=\ev_{I_{j}}
.

A pre-3-Hilbert space is called
Hilbert direct sum complete
(
\boxplus
-complete) if every two objects
a_{1},a_{2}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
admit a Hilbert direct sum.

These isometric equivalences are compatible under composition, showing that the space of Hilbert direct sums of
a_{1},a_{2}
is isometrically contractible.

Remark 4.19
.

The notion of Hilbert direct sum is strictly stronger than orthogonal direct sum.
Consider the full 2-subcategory of
2\mathsf{Hilb}
whose objects are

(\mathsf{Hilb}^{\boxplus n},n\Tr)
for
n\geq 0

with its restricted UAF given by unitary adjunction and spherical weight given by Sub-Example
4.8
.
This 2-subcategory admits orthogonal direct sums, but not Hilbert direct sums.
In particular, the adjoint functors
I_{j}:\mathsf{Hilb}\to\mathsf{Hilb}\boxplus\mathsf{Hilb}
and
P_{j}:\mathsf{Hilb}\boxplus\mathsf{Hilb}\to\mathsf{Hilb}
are not unitary adjoints with respect to the scaled traces.

Example 4.20
.

Given an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
, the pre-3-Hilbert space
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
from Example
4.7
admits Hilbert direct sums.
Moreover, every
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})\in\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is a Hilbert direct sum of simple modules.
In particular, these results hold for
2\mathsf{Hilb}
.

Example 4.21
.

Given a pre-3-Hilbert space
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
and
a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
,
the linking algebra

{\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})=\boxplus_{i,j=1}^{n}{\mathfrak{X}}(a_{j}\to a_{i})

is the Hilbert direct sum of the 2-Hilbert spaces
{\mathfrak{X}}(a_{j}\to a_{i})
.

Remark 4.22
.

If the pre-3-Hilbert space
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
is Hilbert direct sum complete, then the linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}(a_{1},\dots,a_{n})
(which is organically an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category by Example
4.5
) is isometrically equivalent to
\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(\boxplus a_{i})
.

Lemma 4.23
.

Suppose
F:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
is a unitary functor between pre-3-Hilbert spaces.
If
F
preserves the UAFs, then
F
maps (co)isometries to (co)isometries.
In particular, if
F
preserves the UAFs, then
F
preserves Hilbert direct sums.

Proof.

Since
F
preserves identity 2-morphisms, daggers, and the UAFs, it preserves the (co)isometry relations from Definition
4.10
.
In particular,
F
preserves the relation

\ev_{1}\ev_{1}^{\dagger}+\ev_{2}\ev_{2}^{\dagger}=\id,

and thus
F
preserves Hilbert direct sums.
∎

Construction 4.24

(Hilbert direct sum completion)
.

Given a pre-3-Hilbert space
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
, its
Hilbert direct sum completion
is defined similarly to the matrix category of
{\mathfrak{X}}
defined in
[
Ver22
]
.
It has

•

objects finite lists
(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})
of objects of
{\mathfrak{X}}
,

•

1-morphisms
(a_{1},\dots,a_{t})\to(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})
are formal matrices
X=(X_{ij}:a_{i}\to b_{j})
of 1-morphisms in
{\mathfrak{X}}

•

2-morphisms
X=(X_{ij})\Rightarrow Y=(Y_{ij})
are formal matrices
f=(f_{ij}:X_{ij}\Rightarrow Y_{ij})
of 2-morphisms in
{\mathfrak{X}}
.

Composition of 2-morphisms happens component-wise, i.e.,
(f\circ g)_{ij}=f_{ij}\circ g_{ij}
.
Composition of 1-morphisms is a matrix multiplication formula taking an orthogonal direct sum over
\otimes_{\mathfrak{X}}
:

(X\otimes Y)_{ik}:=\bigoplus_{j}X_{ij}\otimes_{b_{j}}Y_{jk}\qquad\qquad\text{if}\qquad\qquad\begin{aligned} X:(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})&\to(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})\\
Y:(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})&\to(c_{1},\dots,c_{t}).\end{aligned}

The unit of
(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})
is
\operatorname{diag}(1_{a_{1}},\dots,1_{a_{r}})
.

The UAF of
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
on
X=(X_{ij})
is given
(X^{\vee})_{ij}:=(X^{\vee}_{ji})
and

(\ev_{X}:X^{\vee}\otimes X\Rightarrow 1_{(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})})_{ij}:=\delta_{i=j}\cdot\bigoplus_{k}\ev_{X_{ik}}:X_{ik}^{\vee}\otimes_{a_{k}}X_{ki}\Rightarrow 1_{b_{i}}

and similarly for
\coev_{X}
.
The spherical weight
\Psi^{\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})}
is given on

(f_{ij})\in\End_{\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})}(1_{(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})})=\bigoplus\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(1_{a_{j}})

by
\bigoplus_{j}\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}}_{a_{j}}(f_{jj})
.

To see that this weight is indeed spherical, for
X=(X_{ij}):(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})\to(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})
and
f=(f_{ij})\in\End_{\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})}(X)
,

\Psi^{\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})}_{(b_{1},\dots,b_{s})}(f)=\sum_{i,j}\Psi^{\mathfrak{X}}_{b_{j}}\left(\,\vbox{\hbox{\hbox to58.22pt{\vbox to51.22pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 37.64354pt\lower-25.6073pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@closescope \hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1}

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}}}\right)=\Psi^{\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})}_{(a_{1},\dots,a_{r})}(f).

Observe that
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
comes equipped with an organic isometric inclusion
\iota_{X}:{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
given by
a\mapsto(a)
,
{}_{a}X_{b}\mapsto({}_{a}X_{b})
, and
(f:X\Rightarrow Y)\mapsto(f)
.

Remark 4.25
.

The object
(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\in\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
is manifestly the Hilbert direct sum of
(x_{1}),\dots,(x_{n})\in\iota({\mathfrak{X}})
.

Lemma 4.26
.

\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
is Hilbert direct sum complete.

Proof.

One verifies that the Hilbert direct sum of
(a_{1},\dots,a_{m})
and
(b_{1},\dots,b_{n})
is the concatenation

(a_{1},\dots,a_{m},b_{1},\dots,b_{n})
.
∎

Remark 4.27
.

In fact,
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}
is a
{\dagger}
-3-functor on the
\rm C^{*}
-3-category of pre-3-Hilbert spaces.
We omit the proof which is similar to the proof that Q-system completion is a 3-functor on the
\rm C^{*}
3-category of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-categories from
[
CP22
]
.

The Hilbert direct sum completion satisfies a universal property in terms of the canonical isometric inclusion of pre-3-Hilbert spaces
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}:{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
.

Proposition 4.28
.

For any Hilbert direct sum complete pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{Y}}
,
precomposition with
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is an equivalence of unitary 2-categories

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\xrightarrow{\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}^{*}}\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})

which maps

•

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
onto
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
, and

•

\mathsf{Isom}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
onto
\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.

To prove this proposition, we use the ‘overlay’ graphical calculus for
{\dagger}
-2-functors from
[
CP22
, §2.4]
.
We represent 2-functors
A,B:{\mathfrak{Z}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
by
textured regions
, transformations
\rho,\sigma:A\Rightarrow B
by
textured strings
, and modifications
m:\rho\Rrightarrow\sigma
by coupons.

One should think of this as identifying
{\mathfrak{Z}}\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(*\to{\mathfrak{Z}})
, where
*
is the category with one object
*
, one 1-morphism
1_{*}
, and 2-morphisms
\End(1_{*})={\mathbb{C}}
,
and identifying
A:{\mathfrak{Z}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
with
A\circ-:\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(*\to{\mathfrak{Z}})\to\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(*\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.
We refer the reader to
[
CP22
, §2.4]
for further details.

We now extend the results on dominance and truncation from
[
CP22
, §4.6]
to the setting of pre-3-Hilbert spaces.

Definition 4.29
.

Suppose
{\mathfrak{X}},{\mathfrak{Z}}
are pre-3-Hilbert spaces where
{\mathfrak{Z}}
admits Hilbert direct sums.
A
{\dagger}
2-functor
G:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Z}}
is called

•

\boxplus
-0-dominant
if for all
z\in{\mathfrak{Z}}
, there are

x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and a coisometry

\boxplus G(x_{i})\to z
.

•

\boxplus
-dominant if it is both
\boxplus
-0-dominant and locally dominant, i.e., every hom
{\dagger}
-functor
G_{x\to x^{\prime}}
is dominant (further unpacked, every 1-morphism
{}_{G(x)}Z_{G(x^{\prime})}
is unitarily isomorphic to an orthogonal direct summand of some
{}_{G(x)}G(X)_{G(x^{\prime})}
).

Remark 4.30
.

In the algebraic linear 2-category setting, when
{\mathfrak{X}},{\mathfrak{Z}}
are locally Cauchy complete linear 2-categories such that
{\mathfrak{Z}}
admits direct sums of objects,
\boxplus
-0-dominance means that for every
z\in{\mathfrak{Z}}
, there are
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and a condensation
\boxplus G(x_{i})\mathrel{\,\hskip 3.22916pt\joinrel\rhook\joinrel\hskip-3.22916pt\joinrel\rightarrow}z
.
When
{\mathfrak{X}},{\mathfrak{Z}}
are unitary 2-categories such that
{\mathfrak{Z}}
admits orthogonal direct sums, we modify the algebraic definition above by using orthogonal direct sums and
{\dagger}
-condensations.

Lemma 4.31
.

Suppose
{\mathfrak{X}},{\mathfrak{Z}}
are pre-3-Hilbert spaces where
{\mathfrak{Z}}
admits Hilbert direct sums.
If a
{\dagger}
-2-functor
G:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Z}}
is
\boxplus
-0-dominant, then

-\circ G:\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{Z}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\to\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})

is faithful on 2-morphisms.
If
G
is
\boxplus
-dominant, then
-\circ G
is fully faithful on 2-morphisms.

Proof.

To prove the first result, we modify the proof of
[
CP22
, Prop. 4.10]
using
\boxplus
-0-dominance instead of
0
-dominance.
The second result is then a straightforward adaptation of
[
CP22
, Prop. 4.11]
mutatis mutandis which we leave to the reader.

Suppose
A,B\in\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{Z}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
,
\rho,\sigma:A\Rightarrow B
, and
m:\rho\Rrightarrow\sigma
, all represented graphically as in (
19
).
We prove that if
m\circ G=0
, then
m=0
.
As
G
is
\boxplus
-0-dominant,
for each
z\in{\mathfrak{Z}}
, there are
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and a coisometry

Proof of Proposition
4.28
.

The proof is similar to the proof of the universal property of Q-system completion from
[
CP22
, §4]
.

Since every object of
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
is a Hilbert direct sum of objects in the image of
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
,
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is
\boxplus
-0-dominant.
By Lemma
4.31
,
-\circ\iota
is faithful on 2-morphisms.

Observe that
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is a local
{\dagger}
-equivalence.
Again by Lemma
4.31
,
-\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is fully faithful on 2-morphisms.

We now show

-\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is a
{\dagger}
-equivalence on hom-categories.
It remains to prove essential surjectivity on hom-categories.
Suppose we have a 2-transformation
\rho:A\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}\Rightarrow B\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
for two functors
A,B:\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
.
We construct a 2-transformation
\sigma:A\Rightarrow B
such that
\sigma\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}\cong\rho
.
For each
x_{1},\dots,x_{n}\in{\mathfrak{X}}
,

(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\in\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
is the Hilbert direct sum
\boxplus\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}(x_{j})
.
Hence we have a canonical isometric equivalence
A(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\cong\boxplus A(x_{j})

(where we abbreviate
A(x_{j}):=(A\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}})(x_{j})
) whose canonical isometries are denoted by
I_{j}^{A(x)}:A(x_{j})\to A(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})
, and similarly for
B
.
We define
\sigma_{(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})}:=\bigoplus{I^{A(x)}_{j}}^{\vee}\otimes\rho_{x_{j}}\otimes I^{B(x)}_{j}:\boxplus A(x_{j})\to\boxplus B(x_{j})
, which we represent graphically by

\sigma_{(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})}=\bigoplus\vbox{\hbox{\hbox to91.05pt{\vbox to29.25pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 48.3696pt\lower-14.62637pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@closescope \hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1}

-\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
restricted to
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
is essentially surjective onto
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}).

Notice that
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is UAF-preserving. Since the composite of UAF-preserving functors is again UAF-preserving, the restriction of
\iota^{*}_{\mathfrak{X}}
is well-defined.

Now, if
A\in\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
, it is clear that
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}(A)
is UAF-preserving. Since
\iota_{{\mathfrak{Y}}}^{-1}
is also UAF-preserving, we thus have that the lift
\iota_{{\mathfrak{Y}}}^{-1}\circ\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathcal{A}})
of
A
is UAF-preserving.

-\circ\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
restricted to
\mathsf{Isom}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
is essentially surjective onto
\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.

Notice that
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is in fact isomtetric. Since the composite of isomtetric functors is again isometric, the restriction of
\iota^{*}_{\mathfrak{X}}
is well-defined.

Now if
A\in\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
, it is clear that
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}(A)
is isometric.
Since
\iota_{\mathfrak{Y}}^{-1}
can be taken to be the isometric ‘evaluation’ functor
\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{Y}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
given by
(y_{1},\dots,y_{n})\mapsto\boxplus y_{j}
as
{\mathfrak{Y}}
is Hilbert direct sum complete, we conclude that the lift
\iota_{{\mathfrak{Y}}}^{-1}\circ\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathcal{A}})
of
A
is isometric.
∎

Remark 4.32
.

We expect that the universal property in Proposition
4.28
may be stated in terms of an isometric equivalence of pre-3-Hilbert spaces in certain cases.
In order to do so, one would need an organic pre-3-Hilbert space structure on
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.
We refer the reader to §
5.3
below for further discussion.

4.3.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monads and
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad completeness

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
in a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is an object
a\in{\mathfrak{X}}
together with an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
({}_{a}A_{a},\mu,\iota)\in\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(a)
. Notice when
{\mathfrak{X}}
is the delooping
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}
for an H*-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
, the H*-monads in
{\mathfrak{X}}
correspond to the H*-algebras in
{\mathcal{C}}
.

Example 4.33
.

Given an object
a
in a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
, any summand of
1_{a}
has a canonical structure of a standard Q-system.

Example 4.34
.

Similar to Example
3.20
, for any 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}
,

{}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}
has a canonical structure of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
with multiplication and unit given by

\mu:=\id_{X}\otimes\ev_{X}\otimes\id_{X^{\vee}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\iota:=\coev_{X}.

When
{}_{a}X_{b}
is a coisometry,
{}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}
is a standard Q-system as
\ev_{X}\ev^{\dagger}_{X}=\id_{1_{b}}
.

Definition 4.35
.

A
splitting

of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
A\in{\mathfrak{X}}(a\to a)
in a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is
an object
b\in{\mathfrak{X}}

and a 1-morphism
{}_{a}X_{b}
such that
\ev_{X}\ev_{X}^{\dagger}\in\End(1_{b})
is invertible
together with a unitary algebra isomorphism
u:{}_{a}A_{a}\to{}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}
.

We say a pre-3-Hilbert space is
idempotent complete
if every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra splits.

Remark 4.36
.

If
({}_{a}X_{b},u)
splits the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
{}_{a}A_{a}
,
then
X
is canonically a unital left
A
-module and
X^{\vee}
is canonically a unital right
A
-module where

Lemma 4.37
.

In an idempotent complete pre-3-Hilbert space, every object is isometrically equivalent to a Hilbert direct sum of simple objects.

Proof.

Let
a
be an object in an idempotent complete pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
.
We can write
1_{a}=\bigoplus 1_{i}
as an orthogonal direct sum of simple objects in the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
\End(a)
.
Each
1_{i}
has the structure of a standard Q-system with multiplication
\mu_{i}
and unit
\iota_{i}
given by the canonical isomorphism and isometry

\mu_{i}:=1_{i}\otimes 1_{i}\xrightarrow{\cong}1_{i}\qquad\qquad\iota_{i}:=1_{\mathfrak{X}}\xrightarrow{\coev_{1_{i}}}1_{i}\otimes 1_{i}\xrightarrow{\cong}1_{i}.

Since
{\mathfrak{X}}
is idempotent complete, we have objects
a_{i}
and 1-morphisms
{}_{a}(X_{i})_{a_{i}}
such that
\ev_{X_{i}}\ev_{X_{i}}^{\dagger}
is invertible, together with a unitary unital algebra maps
u_{i}:1_{i}\to{}_{a}X_{i}\otimes_{a_{i}}(X_{i})_{a}^{\vee}
.
Unitality of
u_{i}
implies that

\vbox{\hbox{\hbox to53.8pt{\vbox to52.65pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 25.87187pt\lower-31.69609pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke=#000000} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill=#000000} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width=0.4pt} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \lxSVG@closescope \hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1}
\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{}{{}}{}

{}{{}}{}{}{}{}{{}}{}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin=1} \color[rgb]{0.8,1,0.8}\lxSVG@fill\lxSVG@drawpath@unclipped{M -35.43 -43.31 M -35.43 -43.31 L -35.43 27.56 L 35.43 27.56 L 35.43 -43.31 Z M 35.43 27.56}{stroke:none} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces

so
\coev_{X_{i}}
is manifestly a coisometry satisfying
\coev_{X_{i}}^{\dagger}\coev_{X_{i}}=p_{i}
, the orthogonal projection onto
1_{i}
.
It immediately follows that
\sum\coev_{X_{i}}^{\dagger}\coev_{X_{i}}=\sum p_{i}=\id_{1_{a}}
.
By (
17
), we also get that
\ev_{X_{i}}
is also an isometry.
Since
{}_{a}X_{i}\otimes_{a_{i}}(X_{i})_{a}^{\vee}
is a standard Q-system, we see that
\ev_{X_{i}}\ev_{X_{i}}^{\dagger}=\id_{a_{i}}
.
Thus each
X_{i}
is a coisometry and
\sum\coev^{\dagger}_{X_{i}}\coev_{X_{i}}=\id_{1_{a}}
, so the
X_{i}
witness
a
as the Hilbert direct sum
\boxplus a_{i}
.
∎

Warning 4.38
.

When
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a finite idempotent complete 3-Hilbert space, there are infinitely many isometric equivalence classes of simple objects.
For example,
2\mathsf{Hilb}
has infinitely many simples
(\mathsf{Hilb},r\Tr)
for
r>0
up to isometric equivalence.

Construction 4.39

(
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad completion)
.

Similar to the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra completion of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category from Definition
3.22
, we may take the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
monad completion

\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
of a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
.
Again, it is closely related to the Q-system completion
\mathsf{QSys}({\mathfrak{X}})
from
[
CHPJP22
]
, but we must now correct for bubbles.
As before,

•

the objects are

{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monads

(a,{}_{a}A_{a})
in
{\mathfrak{X}}
,

•

1-morphisms
{}_{A}M_{B}:A\to B
are
{}_{a}A_{a}-{}_{b}B_{b}
bimodules (these can be interpreted as
A
-
B
bimodules in the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-linking algebra
{\mathcal{L}}(a,b)
), and

•

2-morphisms are intertwiners.

Composition of 2-morphisms is composition of intertwiners.
Composition of 1-morphisms is the relative product achieved by splitting the appropriate separability idempotent.
As before,
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
carries a canonical UAF given by choosing
\delta=0
in (
10
).

We now endow

Hence
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
is a pre-3-Hilbert space.

Moreover, there is a canonical isometric embedding
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}:{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
by
a\mapsto 1_{a}
.

.

Hence the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra
{}_{a}A_{a}
is adjoint equivalent to the standard Q-system
1_{b}
in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
.

Lemma 4.41
.

A pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is idempotent complete if and only if the canonical isometric inclusion
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}:{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
is isometrically essentially surjective and thus an isometric equivalence of pre-3-Hilbert spaces.

Proof.

If
{\mathfrak{X}}
is idempotent complete, then every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
{}_{a}A_{a}
splits.
By Remark
4.40
, any splitting
({}_{a}X_{b},u)
can be promoted to an isometric adjoint equivalence
({}_{A}X_{1_{b}},u)
, and thus every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad is in the isometric essential image of the canonical isometric inclusion
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}:{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
.

Conversely, if
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is isometrically essentially surjective, then given any
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
{}_{a}A_{a}
in
{\mathfrak{X}}
, there is an isometric adjoint equivalence
{}_{A}X_{1_{b}}
between
{}_{a}A_{a}
and a standard Q-system
1_{b}
in the image of
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
.
A standard calculation shows that
X
splits
{}_{a}A_{a}
.
∎

Lemma 4.42
.

The
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra completion
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
of a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is idempotent complete.

Proof.

The proof is entirely similar to
[
CHPJP22
, Cor. 3.37]
; one shows that if
{}_{A}B_{A}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
where
{}_{a}A_{a}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad in
{\mathfrak{X}}
, then
{}_{a}B_{a}
already has an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad structure in
{\mathfrak{X}}
, and
{}_{A}B_{B}
splits
{}_{A}B_{A}
in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
.
∎

We now state the universal property of
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
which is similar to the universal property of Q-system completion from
[
CP22
]
(see also
[
Déc22
]
).
The proof is entirely similar to the above proof and the proof of Proposition
4.28
, so we will not include it here.

Proposition 4.43
.

For any idempotent complete pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{Y}}
,
precomposition with
\iota_{\mathfrak{X}}
is an equivalence of unitary 2-categories

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\xrightarrow{\iota^{*}}\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})

which maps

•

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
onto
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
, and

•

\mathsf{Isom}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
onto
\mathsf{Isom}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.

Finally, the next result shows that Hilbert direct sum completeness is preserved by taking the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad completion.

Proposition 4.44
.

If
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a Hilbert direct sum complete pre-3-Hilbert space, then
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
is also Hilbert direct sum complete.

Proof.

Suppose
{}_{a}A_{a}
and
{}_{b}B_{b}
are
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monads in
{\mathfrak{X}}
.
Then there are canonical isometries
I_{a}:a\to a\boxplus b
and
I_{b}:b\to a\boxplus b
, and we can form the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad

A\boxplus B:=I_{a}^{\vee}\otimes_{a}A\otimes_{a}I_{a}\oplus I_{b}^{\vee}\otimes_{b}B\otimes_{b}I_{b}

with component-wise multiplication and unit.
A straightforward calculation shows that

A\otimes_{a}I_{a}:a\to a\boxplus b
is an
A
-
A\boxplus B
bimodule which is an isometry in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
,
and similarly for
B\otimes_{b}I_{b}:b\to a\boxplus b
as a
B
-
A\boxplus B
bimodule,
and that
A\otimes_{a}I_{a},B\otimes_{b}I_{b}
witness

A\boxplus B
as the Hilbert direct sum of
A
and
B
in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
.
∎

4.4.
3-Hilbert spaces

We are finally ready to introduce the notion of a 3-Hilbert space.

Definition 4.45
.

A pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is called a
3-Hilbert space
if it admits Hilbert direct sums and all
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras split.
The notion of isometric equivalence of 3-Hilbert spaces is the same as that for pre-3-Hilbert spaces.

Remark 4.46
.

The underlying 2-category of a 3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
is finite semisimple.
To see this, it suffices to show that every unital condensation monad
{}_{a}A_{a}
in
{\mathfrak{X}}
the sense of
[
DR18
]
splits.
By
[
GYZ24
]
, every finite semisimple module category over a unitary multifusion category is uniquely unitarizable.
Hence,
A
is equivalent to a standard Q-system in the unitary multifusion category
\End(a)
, and we know every standard Q-system splits.
In the spirit of this paper, we provide a manifestly unitary approach to these results in Proposition
5.7
and Corollary
5.11
.

Definition 4.47
.

If
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
is a pre-3-Hilbert space, then
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}}))
is a 3-Hilbert space by Lemmas
4.26
and
4.42
and Proposition
4.44
. We denote this unitary Cauchy completion 3-Hilbert space by
\textup{\textcent}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}})
.

Example 4.48
.

If
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category,
then the 2-category

\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in
{\mathcal{C}}
is a 3-Hilbert space as it already admits Hilbert direct sums.
Indeed, if
A,B\in{\mathcal{C}}
are
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras, then
as in the proof of Proposition
4.44
,

{}_{A}(A\oplus B)_{A\oplus B}
and
{}_{B}(A\oplus B)_{A\oplus B}
witness
A\oplus B
as a Hilbert direct sum of
A,B
in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
.

Example 4.49
.

If
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category,
then
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is also a 3-Hilbert space.
We already saw that
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
admits Hilbert direct sums in Example
4.20
above.
To see that every
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad splits, observe that
by Theorem
3.28
and Example
4.13
, the functor
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
from §
3.5
is automatically isometrically essentially surjective, as every
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
is isometrically adjoint equivalent to a
{\mathcal{C}}
-module of the form
({\mathcal{C}}_{A},\Tr^{{\mathcal{C}}_{A}})
.
Hence one can pull back an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad from

\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
to
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
and split it in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
.
Since the functor
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
preserves the UAF, pushing forward the splitting achieves our goal.

Theorem 4.51
.

Suppose
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
The unitary equivalence
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})

from §
3.5

is an isometric equivalence of 3-Hilbert spaces.

Proof.

The unitary 2-equivalence
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
preserves the UAF and is isometrically essentially surjective by Theorem
3.28
and Example
4.13
.
It remains to prove it is isometric.
On each component, we know that the unitary equivalence

\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
must
map

\Psi^{\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})}

to

\Psi^{\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}

up to a uniform scalar by Remark
4.50
.
We may thus reduce to the case that
{\mathcal{C}}
is indecomposable.
Again by Remark
4.50
, it suffices to check the values of the
\Psi
s at a single simple object in
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
; we choose the standard Q-system
1_{1}
where
1_{\mathcal{C}}=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{k}1_{j}
is an orthogonal direct sum decomposition into simples.

The corresponding module category in
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is
{\mathcal{C}}_{1}:={\mathcal{C}}\otimes 1_{1}
, the ‘first column’ of
{\mathcal{C}}
where
{\mathcal{C}}
acts on the left.
The trace on
{\mathcal{C}}_{1}
from (
12
) from Proposition
3.25

is exactly

\Tr^{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}}=(\psi_{\mathcal{C}}\circ\tr^{\vee}_{\mathcal{C}})|_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}}
.
Since
\End_{\mathcal{C}}(1_{1})={\mathbb{C}}
, we compute

\displaystyle\Psi^{\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}_{({\mathcal{C}}_{1},\Tr^{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}})}(\id_{\id_{{\mathcal{C}}_{1}}})

\displaystyle\underset{\text{(Ex.~\ref{ex:WeightOnModC})}}{=}\frac{d_{1_{1}}}{\dim({\mathcal{C}}_{1})}\sum_{c\in\Irr({\mathcal{C}}_{1})}d_{c}^{2}=d_{1_{1}}=\Psi^{\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})}_{1_{1}}(\id_{1_{1}})

as claimed.
∎

Corollary 4.52
.

Every 3-Hilbert space is of the form
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
for some
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
.

Proof.

It suffices to consider the case that
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a connected 3-Hilbert space.
Let
a\in{\mathfrak{X}}
be simple, and consider the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}=\Omega_{a}=\End_{\mathfrak{X}}(a)
.
By Proposition
4.43
, precomposition with the canonical isometric inclusion
\iota_{\mathcal{C}}:{\mathcal{C}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
gives a canonical equivalence

\mathsf{Isom}({\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathfrak{X}})\cong\mathsf{Isom}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\to{\mathfrak{X}});

we thus have a canonical fully faithful isometric unitary functor

\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\hookrightarrow{\mathfrak{X}}
; we identify
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
with its image in
{\mathfrak{X}}
.
To see that this functor is isometrically essentially surjective, suppose
b\in{\mathfrak{X}}
and let
{}_{a}X_{b}
be a dualizable 1-morphism.
The
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-monad
A:={}_{a}X\otimes_{b}X^{\vee}_{a}\in\Omega_{a}
splits in
{\mathfrak{X}}
and also defines an object of
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathcal{C}})\subset{\mathfrak{X}}
.
By Remark
4.40
and Lemma
4.41
,
{}_{A}X_{b}
is an isometric adjoint equivalence in
{\mathfrak{X}}
, as desired.
∎

The proof of Theorem
B
follows immediately from Theorem
4.51
and Corollary
4.52
.
∎

5.
The 3-category of 3-Hilbert spaces

In this section, we promote the map
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)\mapsto(\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}),\Psi)

to a unitary equivalence of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-categories

{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Hilb}
.
We refer the reader to
[
Fer
]
for the recently introduced notion of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-category.
In future work, we plan to promote this unitary equivalence to an isometric equivalence of 4-Hilbert spaces.

Definition 5.1
.

The
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-category
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
is given as follows.

•

The objects are the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
.

•

The 1-morphisms
{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}
are simply finite semisimple unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule categories equipped with
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule traces.
The 1-composition operation is the relative Deligne product
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{D}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{E}}
equipped with its unitary trace from Lemma
3.11

or (
8
) depending on the model chosen for the relative Deligne product.

•

The 2-morphisms
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}\Rightarrow{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
are unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule functors with no compatibility requirement with the tracial data.
The 2-composition is composition of functors, which is strictly associative.

•

Given
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule functors
F,G:{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
,
the 3-morphisms
F\Rrightarrow G
are bimodule natural transformations, and 3-composition is the usual composition of natural transformations.

•

The
{\dagger}
-operation on 3-morphisms is the adjoint of natural transformations, which is again a natural transformations.

All coherence data for this 3-category is unitary as discussed in Remark
3.17
.

Remark 5.2
.

Observe that the hom
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-categories in
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
can be equipped with 3-Hilbert space structures by Example
4.7
and the folding trick:

\mathsf{Bim}^{{\dagger}}({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes{\mathcal{D}}^{\rm mp}).

Remark 5.3
.

As the 2-morphisms in
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
are not required to be compatible with the bimodule traces, equivalence for 1-morphisms in
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
is unitary equivalence of the underlying bimodule categories forgetting the tracial data.

Definition 5.4
.

The
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-category
3\mathsf{Hilb}
is given as follows.

•

The objects are the 3-Hilbert spaces
({\mathfrak{X}},\vee,\Psi)
.

•

The 1-morphisms
{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
are the UAF-preserving
{\dagger}
-2-functors.
The 1-composition operation is composition of 2-functors.

•

Given
F,G:{\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}}
, the 2-morphisms
F\Rightarrow G
are
{\dagger}
-2-transformations,
and 2-composition is composition of 2-transformations.

•

Given 2-transformations
\rho,\sigma:F\Rightarrow G
, a 3-morphism
m:\rho\Rrightarrow\sigma
is a 2-modification, and 3-composition is the usual composition of 2-modifications.

•

The
{\dagger}
-operation on 3-morphisms is the adjoint of modifications, which is again a modification due to the unitarity of the source and target
{\dagger}
-2-natural transformations constraint data.

All coherence data for this 3-category is unitary.

Remark 5.5
.

For 3-Hilbert spaces
{\mathfrak{X}}
and
{\mathfrak{Y}}
, we expect
\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
and
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
to be equivalent as unitary 2-categories, but not isometrically so as 3-Hilbert spaces for some putative 3-Hilbert space structure.
Non-pivotal unitary tensor functors between
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories
{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}
provide one obstruction.
By completing
{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}
, these yield 2-functors
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{D}})
which does not preserve UAFs.
However, for every such 2-functor, one may equip
{\mathcal{D}}
with a different
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace such that it will be UAF-preserving.
These have the same underlying 2-functor, and they are unitarily equivalent, but they will not be isometrically so.

5.1.
Unitary 3-equivalence between
3\mathsf{Hilb}
and
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}

We prove Theorem
C
which states that
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}
gives a unitary equivalence between the
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-categories
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
and
3\mathsf{Hilb}
.
We expect this equivalence to be as 4-Hilbert spaces.
Defining a spherical structure and isometries within 4-Hilbert spaces requires a detailed treatment of unitary adjoints for 2-functors, which we leave to future work.

Lemma 5.6
.

Given
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi)
and
({\mathcal{D}},\vee,\psi)
, and a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{N}}

{\dagger}
-2-functor

\scriptstyle m^{\prime}
\scriptstyle n^{\prime}

We now describe the 3-functor
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}\colon{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Hilb}
.
We recall that the non-unitary version
\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Vec}
was shown to be an equivalence in
[
Déc22
, Thm. 2.2.2]
.

•

An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}\in{\mathrm{H}}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
maps to
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\in 3\mathsf{Hilb}
.

•

A unitary finite semisimple
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule category
{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}
with a bimodule trace maps to the UAF-preserving
{\dagger}
-2-functor
-\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}:\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})
.

•

A unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule functor
F:{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}\to{}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
maps to the
{\dagger}
-2-transformation
-\boxtimes F:-\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{D}}\Rightarrow-\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{D}}
.

•

A
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule natural tranformation
\rho:F\Rightarrow G
maps to the 2-modification
-\boxtimes\rho:-\boxtimes F\Rrightarrow-\boxtimes G
.

In fact,
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}\colon{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Hilb}
can be described as the Yoneda map

\displaystyle{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}(\mathsf{Hilb}\to-)\colon{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}

\displaystyle\to 3\mathsf{Hilb}

\displaystyle{\mathcal{C}}

\displaystyle\mapsto{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}(\mathsf{Hilb}\to{\mathcal{C}})=\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}),

which is clearly a (weak)
{\dagger}
-3-functor.

Proof of Theorem
C
.

By Corollary
4.52
, the functor
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}\colon{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to 3\mathsf{Hilb}
is unitarily essentially surjective (even isometrically so!).
It remains to prove it is fully faithful, i.e.

\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}:{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}})\to\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))

is a
{\dagger}
-equivalence on every hom 2-category.

We will use the fact that, viewing
{\mathcal{C}}
as a right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module
{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}\in\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
, Proposition
3.9
yields an isometric equivalence
{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathrm{B}}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{{\mathcal{C}}})
given on hom-spaces by
c\mapsto c\otimes-
.
Moreover, the data of a unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule
{}_{{\mathcal{C}}}{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{D}}}
equipped with a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace
\Tr^{\mathcal{M}}
is precisely the data of a UAF-preserving
{\dagger}
-2-functor

\displaystyle{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}

\displaystyle\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})

\displaystyle\star

\displaystyle\mapsto{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{D}}}

\displaystyle(c\colon\star\to\star)

\displaystyle\mapsto(c\triangleright-\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{D}}}\to{\mathcal{M}}_{{\mathcal{D}}})

In particular, recall that a right
{\mathcal{D}}
-module trace on
{\mathcal{M}}
is a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule trace exactly when
c\triangleright-\dashv_{\dagger}c^{\vee}\triangleright-
for all
c\in{\mathcal{C}}
.
This observation yields an equivalence of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
-2-categories

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))\cong{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}).

(We conjecture this to be an isometric equivalence of 3-Hilbert spaces.
We leave this to future work.)

Moreover, by Proposition
4.43
we know

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathrm{B}}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{{\mathcal{C}}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))

given by restriction to the subcategory
{\mathrm{B}}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{{\mathcal{C}}})
of
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
.
Putting this all together, this defines the pseudo-inverse

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))\to{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}).

We will only unpack this equivalence at the level of functors and bimodules, as the desired facts for higher morphisms follow similarly.
Indeed, given some
F\colon\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})
, we determine a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule
{}_{{\mathcal{C}}}F({\mathcal{C}})_{{\mathcal{D}}}
by

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathrm{B}}{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathrm{B}}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\star}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F({\mathcal{C}})_{\mathcal{D}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}

By Corollary
3.12
,
F({\mathcal{C}})_{\mathcal{D}}\cong{\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}}F({\mathcal{C}})_{\mathcal{D}}
isometrically, hence
F\cong-\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}F({\mathcal{C}})_{\mathcal{D}}
when restricted to
{\mathrm{B}}\End({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})
.
The universal property of
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})={\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{Alg}({\mathcal{C}})
then implies
F\cong-\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}F({\mathcal{C}})_{\mathcal{D}}
isometrically.
∎

5.2.
The forgetful 3-functor
3\mathsf{Hilb}\to 3\mathsf{Vec}
is fully faithful

In this section, we prove Corollary
D
which states that the forgetful functor
3\mathsf{Hilb}\to 3\mathsf{Vec}
is fully faithful.

The unitary equivalence
{\mathcal{M}}\cong{\mathcal{M}}_{1}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}_{11}}{\mathcal{C}}
of right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module categories used in the proof of Corollary
3.13
can also be used to prove that every module category over a unitary multifusion category is unitarizable.
The main ingredient is the fact that every connected separable algebra in a unitary fusion category is equivalent to a Q-system by
[
CGGH23
]
.

Proposition 5.7

(
[
GYZ24
]
)
.

Every finite semisimple module category
{\mathcal{M}}
over a unitary multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
is uniquely unitarizable.

Proof.

The proof proceeds in steps on properties of the module category
{\mathcal{M}}
and the unitary multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
.

If
{\mathcal{C}}
is fusion and
{\mathcal{M}}
is indecomposable,
then
{\mathcal{M}}
is unitarizable by
[
CGGH23
]
.
Indeed,
{\mathcal{M}}
is equivalent to
{}_{A}{\mathcal{C}}
where
A=\underline{\End}_{\mathcal{C}}(m)
for any simple object
m\in{\mathcal{M}}
.
Since
m
is simple,
A
is connected, i.e.,
{\mathcal{C}}(1_{\mathcal{C}}\to A)\cong{\mathcal{M}}(m\to m)={\mathbb{C}}
.
By
[
CGGH23
]
,
A
is equivalent to a Q-system, so there is a Q-system
B\in{\mathcal{C}}
and an equivalence
{\mathcal{M}}\cong{}_{B}{\mathcal{C}}
, which is unitary.

If
{\mathcal{C}}
is fusion and
{\mathcal{M}}
is arbitrary, then
{\mathcal{M}}
is a direct sum of indecomposable module categories.
Each of these indecomposable summands is unitarizable, so
{\mathcal{M}}
is too.

If
{\mathcal{C}}
is indecomposable unitary multifusion and
{\mathcal{M}}
is indecomposable, then

{\mathcal{C}}
is unitarily Morita equivalent to any of its unitary fusion corners of the form
{\mathcal{C}}_{ii}=1_{i}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\otimes 1_{i}
for a simple
1_{i}\subseteq 1_{\mathcal{C}}
.
Consider
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}:={\mathcal{M}}\otimes 1_{1}\in\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}}_{11})
.
Since
{\mathcal{C}}_{11}
is unitary fusion, every module category is unitarizable by Step 2, so we may assume
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}
is unitary.
Since
{\mathcal{M}}
is indecomposable,
{\mathcal{M}}
is equivalent as a right
{\mathcal{C}}
-module category to the unitary relative Deligne product
{\mathcal{M}}_{1}\boxtimes_{{\mathcal{C}}_{11}}{\mathcal{C}}

[
BBJ19
]
,
[
GMP+23
, Prop. 3.12]
, which is again unitary.
Hence
{\mathcal{M}}
is unitarizable.

If
{\mathcal{C}}
is multifusion and
{\mathcal{M}}
is arbitrary, then
{\mathcal{M}}
is a direct sum of indecomposable module categories.
Each of these indecomposable summands is unitarizable, so
{\mathcal{M}}
is too.

This follows from
[
Reu23
, Rem. 4]
which also applies to Theorem 8 therein.
∎

By the folding trick, we get the following immediate corollary.

Corollary 5.8
.

For unitary multifusion categories
{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}
, every finite semisimple
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule category is uniquely unitarizable.

We also have the following immediate corollary about unitarizability of finite semisimple 2-categories.

Corollary 5.9
.

If a finite semisimple 2-category
{\mathfrak{X}}
is unitarizable (is equivalent to the underlying 2-category of a
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-category),
then it is uniquely unitarizable.
That is, if
{\mathfrak{Y}},{\mathfrak{Z}}
are two
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-categories whose underlying 2-categories are equivalent to
{\mathfrak{X}}
, then
{\mathfrak{Y}}
is unitarily equivalent to
{\mathfrak{Z}}
.

Proof.

By
[
DR18
, Thm. 1.4.9]
, there is a multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
such that
{\mathfrak{X}}
is equivalent to
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
.
Observe that
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
is unitarizable if and only if
{\mathcal{C}}
is unitarizable.
Indeed, if
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
is unitarizable, then so is
\End({\mathcal{C}}_{\mathcal{C}})\cong{\mathcal{C}}
.
Conversely, if
{\mathcal{C}}
is unitarizable, then
\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
is equivalent to
\mathsf{Mod}({\mathcal{C}})
by Proposition
5.7
.
By
[
Reu23
, Rem. 4]
, a unitarizable multifusion category is uniquely unitarizable.
The result now follows from the equivalence
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\cong 3\mathsf{Hilb}
.
∎

Proposition
5.7
affords a second quick proof of the corollary from
[
GYZ24
]
that every separable algebra in a unitary multifusion category is equivalent to a Q-system.
Our proof relies on Sub-Example
3.21
which used unitary adjunction to prove that the internal end
[m,m]_{\mathcal{C}}
has a canonical
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra structure.
We remark that unitary adjunction is implicitly used in the proof of
[
GYZ24
]
, where certain adjunction isomorphims are first shown to be unitary; our approach is manifestly unitary.

Lemma 5.10
.

A separable algebra
A
in a unitary multifusion category
{\mathcal{C}}
is equivalent to a standard Q-system if and only if its category of right modules
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is unitarizable.

Proof.

For a Q-system
A
,
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is well-known to be unitarizable, e.g., see
[
CHPJP22
, §3.2]
.
On the other hand, if
A
is an algebra in
{\mathcal{C}}
such that
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
is unitarizable, there exists a faithful
{\mathcal{C}}
-module trace on
{\mathcal{C}}_{A}
by Corollary
3.13
.
By Sub-Example
3.21
, the internal end

[A,A]_{\mathcal{C}}
has a canonical
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra structure, and it is well-known to be isomorphic as an algebra to
A
(perhaps non-unitarily).
Finally,
[A,A]_{\mathcal{C}}
is equivalent to a Q-system by Fact
(A2)
.
∎

Corollary 5.11
.

Every separable algebra is equivalent to a standard Q-system.

Proof.

Immediate from Proposition
5.7
and Lemma
5.10
.
∎

Lemma 5.12
.

Given any two finite semisimple unitary
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule categories
{\mathcal{M}},{\mathcal{N}}
, the forgetful functor

\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}-{\mathcal{D}}}^{{\dagger}}({\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{N}})\to\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}-{\mathcal{D}}}({\mathcal{M}}\to{\mathcal{N}})
is an equivalence.

Proof.

By the folding trick, it suffices to prove the forgetful functor

\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}}^{{\dagger}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})

is an equivalence for right
{\mathcal{C}}
-modules.
If we only cared about
{\mathcal{C}}
-module equivalences, this would follow directly from
[
Reu23
, Prop. 2.11]
, but the proof there does not obviously generalize to general
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functors.
Instead, we note that the category of (unitary)
{\mathcal{C}}
-module functors is a model for the (unitary) relative Deligne product
[
ENO10
, §3]
, and we have a commuting square

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes^{\dagger}_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}^{\rm op}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{M}}\boxtimes_{\mathcal{C}}{\mathcal{N}}^{\rm op}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{Fun}_{{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{M}}_{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathcal{C}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}

where the top left corner denotes the unitary relative Deligne product.
One can show that the top forgetful functor is an equivalence using the ladder category model of the relative Deligne product
[
BBJ19
]
(see also
[
HPT23
, §3]
), and thus the bottom forgetful functor is also an equivalence.
∎

Corollary 5.13
.

The forgetful functor
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to\mathsf{mFC}
is fully faithful.

Proof.

Suppose
{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}
are
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories.
The 2-functor
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}})\to\mathsf{mFC}({\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}})
is fully faithful by Lemma
5.12

and essentially surjective by Corollary
5.8
, which states that
every finite semisimple
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule category is uniquely unitarizable.
∎

Remark 5.14
.

The reader may be worried here that the existence of distinct
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule traces on a
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{D}}
bimodule category may be a counter-example to the forgetful functor
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to\mathsf{mFC}
being fully faithful.
However, equivalence of 1-morphisms is determined by existence of a 2-isomorphism, and the 2-morphisms in
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
are not required to be compatible with bimodule traces.

Proof of Corollary
D
.

By commutativity of the diagram

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathsf{mFC}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 3\mathsf{Hilb}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 3\mathsf{Vec}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Forget}

it suffices to prove that the top arrow is fully faithful.
This is exactly the content of Corollary
5.13
.
∎

5.3.
Is
3\mathsf{Hilb}
enriched in 3-Hilbert spaces?

We end this section with an question on 3-Hilbert spaces that we will consider in the future.
In light of Example
2.15
which gives an organic 2-Hilbert space structure on dagger functors between 2-Hilbert spaces, we ask:

Question 5.15
.

Suppose
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a pre-3-Hilbert space and
{\mathfrak{Y}}
is a 3-Hilbert space.
Is there an organic 3-Hilbert space structure on
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
?

Here are several desiderata for this putative 3-Hilbert space structure on
\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})
.

•

By the universal properties in Propositions
4.28
and
4.43
, we have a unitary equivalence

\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{\dagger}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}}))\to{\mathfrak{Y}}),

which preserves UAF-preserving functors and isometries,
so we may consider the case that
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a 3-Hilbert space.
Given
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories
{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}
and isometric equivalences

{\mathfrak{X}}\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})
and
{\mathfrak{Y}}\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}})
,
the unitary 2-equivalence

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}})\to\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{D}}))\underset{\text{(\lx@sectionsign\ref{sec:3Hilb==H*mFC})}}{\cong}\mathsf{Bim}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})\cong\mathsf{Mod}^{\dagger}({\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes{\mathcal{D}}^{\rm mp})

should be an isometric equivalence where the latter category is equipped with the renormalized 3-Hilbert space structure from Example
4.7
.

•

Given a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
,
the Yoneda embedding
{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}^{\op}\to 2\mathsf{Hilb})

should be isometric.
Moreover, the Yoneda embedding should be an isometric equivalence if and only if
{\mathfrak{X}}
is a 3-Hilbert space.

•

For a pre-3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{X}}
and a 3-Hilbert space
{\mathfrak{Y}}
,
precomposition with
{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})
should be an isometric equivalence

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{Hilb}_{\boxplus}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}}),

and
precomposition with
{\mathfrak{X}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})
should be an isometric equivalence

\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}({\mathfrak{X}}\to{\mathfrak{Y}})\cong\mathsf{Fun}^{{\dagger},\vee}(\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathfrak{X}})\to{\mathfrak{Y}}).

6.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion categories are the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}

In this section, we prove Theorem
E
which asserts a unitary equivalence of
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
3-categories
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\cong 3\mathsf{Hilb}
.

which endow
\mu^{R}
with the structure of an
A
-
A
bimodule functor such that
\eta_{\mu},\varepsilon_{\mu}
witness an adjunction of
A
-
A
bimodule functors.
Observe that rigidity of an algebra is also a property and not additional structure; the space of choices of
\mu^{R}
is contractible.

A rigid algebra is called
separable
if for any choice of
\mu^{R}
, the counit
\varepsilon_{\mu}
admits a splitting as an
A
-
A
bimodule natural transformation, i.e., there exists
\delta:\id_{A}\Rightarrow\mu\circ\mu^{R}
such that
\varepsilon\circ\delta=\id_{\id_{A}}
.
Observe that separability is
independent
of the choice of
\mu^{R}
.

Remark 6.2
.

It may appear that choices of Frobeniators
\theta,\kappa
for
\mu^{R}
as in (
23
) are additional structure.
It was pointed out to us by David Reutter that the Frobeniator
\kappa
is determined by
\alpha
and the adjunction data by the following commuting diagram:

\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\kappa}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\eta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varepsilon}
\kappa
an
{\mathcal{A}}-{\mathcal{A}}
bimod nat iso

zig-zag
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\kappa}
\scriptstyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\varepsilon}

That the lower right triangle commutes is best seen by inverting the bottom associator arrow.
A similar statement holds for
\theta
.

Example 6.3
.

The rigid algebras in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Vec}
are exactly the multifusion categories
[
JF22
, §II]
.
We provide a complete proof below summarized in Corollary
6.7
.
Construction
6.4
constructs a monoidal product on
|{\mathcal{A}}|:=\Hom(\mathsf{Vec}\to{\mathcal{A}})
for any algebra
{\mathcal{A}}\in 2\mathsf{Vec}
, and it is straightforward to prove that the canonical equivalence
|{\mathcal{A}}|\to{\mathcal{A}}
given by evaluation at
{\mathbb{C}}
is monoidal.
When
{\mathcal{A}}
is rigid, we construct explicit evaluation and coevaluation morphisms on
|{\mathcal{A}}|
and we prove they satisfy the zig-zag identities in Proposition
6.5
.

Our main reason for providing the explicit detail below is that we will check later in Section
6.2
that the duals constructed above give a UDF on
|{\mathcal{A}}|
in the unitary setting.

Our construction bears many similarities with
[
JPR23
]
.

In Proposition
6.5
below, we prove that the zig-zag axiom is satisfied.
Thus
|A|
is a rigid finitely semisimple monoidal category, i.e., a multifusion category.

Proposition 6.5
.

Suppose
A
is a rigid algebra in a
\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid
{\mathfrak{C}}
in which all 1-morphisms admit right adjoints.
The monoidal category
|A|={\mathfrak{C}}(1_{\mathfrak{C}}\to A)
from Construction
6.4
above is rigid.

Proof.

All that remains is to verify the zig-zag axioms.
We explicitly prove the relation
(\id_{a}\otimes\ev^{L}_{a})\circ(\coev^{L}_{a}\otimes\id_{a})=\id_{a}
; the other 3 relations are left to the reader.

The zig-zag relation follows from commutativity of the diagram in Figure
2
below; the composite map along the outside of the diagram is the zig-zag formula, and each 2-cell commutes.

which is the identity as claimed.
∎

We have the following immediate corollary.

Corollary 6.6
.

Suppose
A
is a rigid algebra in a
\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid
{\mathfrak{C}}
in which all hom categories are finitely semisimple linear categories, and all 1-morphisms admit right adjoints.
The semisimple tensor category
|A|={\mathfrak{C}}(1_{\mathfrak{C}}\to A)
from Construction
6.4
above is a multifusion category.
When
A
is
connected
(the unit
\iota\in{\mathfrak{C}}(1_{\mathfrak{C}}\to A)
is simple),
|A|
is fusion.

To connect Construction
6.4
with the classification of rigid algebras in
2\mathsf{Vec}
, we note that for an algebra
({\mathcal{A}},\mu,\alpha,1_{\mathcal{A}},\lambda,\rho)\in 2\mathsf{Vec}
,
we have a monoidal equivalence

{\mathcal{A}}\cong|{\mathcal{A}}|:=\mathsf{Fun}(\mathsf{Vec}\to{\mathcal{A}})

intertwining the monoidal structure
\mu
and the monoidal structure from Construction
6.4
.

Corollary 6.7
.

Rigid algebras
({\mathcal{A}},\mu,\alpha,1_{\mathcal{A}},\lambda,\rho)\in 2\mathsf{Vec}
are exactly multifusion categories.

Proof.

Every multifusion category gives a rigid algebra in
2\mathsf{Vec}
as the 2-category of
{\mathcal{A}}
-
{\mathcal{A}}
bimodules, bimodule functors, and bimodule natural transformations admits adjoints.
The converse direction is exactly Construction
6.4
above, noting that if
{\mathcal{A}}\in 2\mathsf{Vec}
, then
{\mathcal{A}}\cong|{\mathcal{A}}|
.
∎

6.2.
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}

In this section, we assume
2\mathsf{Hilb}
is a
{\sf C}^{*}\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid by
[
Fer
]
; we refer the reader to that article for the definition.

We now give a definition of an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}
in the more general setting of a
{\sf C}^{*}\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid
whose underlying strict
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-category is a pre-3-Hilbert space.
We expect the following definition can be generalized to any unitary multifusion 2-category, a notion which will be defined in future work.

Definition 6.8
.

Suppose
{\mathfrak{C}}
is a
{\sf C}^{*}\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid
whose underlying strict
{\mathrm{C}}^{*}
2-category is a pre-3-Hilbert space.
An
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-
algebra
in
{\mathfrak{C}}
is a unital algebra

(A,\mu,\alpha,\iota,\lambda,\rho)

such that

(
{\mathrm{H}}^{enumi}
0)

(Unitary) the 2-isomorphisms
\alpha,\lambda,\rho
are all unitary.

(
{\mathrm{H}}^{enumi}
1)

(Unitarily rigid) the unitary adjoint
\mu^{*}
of
\mu
is an
A
-
A
bimodule functor (which is a property by Remark
6.2
) and the unit
\eta_{\mu}:\id_{A}\Rightarrow\mu^{*}\circ\mu
and counit
\varepsilon_{\mu}:\mu\circ\mu^{*}\Rightarrow\id_{A}
are
A
-
A
bimodule natural transformations.

(
{\mathrm{H}}^{enumi}
2)

(Unitarily separable)
\varepsilon_{\mu}^{\dagger}
is an
A
-
A
bimodule natural transformation and the bubble on the
A
-sheet
\varepsilon_{\mu}\circ\varepsilon_{\mu}^{\dagger}:\id_{A}\Rightarrow\id_{A}
is invertible.

(
{\mathrm{H}}^{enumi}
3)

(Standard) for all
\alpha:\id_{A}\Rightarrow\id_{A}
, we have

Remark 6.9
.

Recall that the standardness condition
(

H
enumi

3)
in Section
3.3
is identical to the sphericality of
\psi
with evaluation
constructed from the counit and multiplcation (
\ev=i^{\dagger}\mu
)
and the coevaluation
constructed from the unit and comultiplcation (
\coev=\mu^{\dagger}i
).
If we similarly modify the notion of sphericality in
[
DR18
, §2.3]
, we obtain the condition
(

H
enumi

3)
above.
David Reutter has made the intriguing suggestion that the non-unitary analog of
(

H
enumi

3)
may be automatic in a fusion 2-category.

Proposition 6.10
.

Every
({\mathcal{C}},\vee,\psi_{\mathcal{C}})\in{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra in
{\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb}
.

Proof.

To see that
{\mathcal{C}}
is unitarily rigid, we note that the category of
{\mathcal{C}}
-
{\mathcal{C}}
unitary bimodules equipped with bimodule traces, unitary bimodule functors, and bimodule natural transformations admits adjoints, and in particular, unitary adjoints.

To see that
{\mathcal{C}}
is unitarily separable, we
work in the category
\End^{\dagger}_{{\mathcal{C}}\text{-}{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{C}}\oplus{\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes{\mathcal{C}})
,
which is equivalent to
\End_{{\mathcal{C}}\text{-}{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{C}}\oplus{\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes{\mathcal{C}})
by Lemma
5.12
.
Since every multifusion category is separable,
\varepsilon_{\mu}
admits a right inverse
\delta_{\mu}:\id_{{\mathcal{C}}}\Rightarrow\otimes\circ\otimes^{*}
in the latter category, and thus in the former.
Since
\End^{\dagger}_{{\mathcal{C}}\text{-}{\mathcal{C}}}({\mathcal{C}}\oplus{\mathcal{C}}\boxtimes{\mathcal{C}})\cong\mathsf{Hilb}^{\oplus n}
for some finite
n
,
the argument of Remark
(A4)
applies, i.e.,
\varepsilon_{\mu}
admits a right inverse if and only if
\varepsilon_{\mu}\circ\varepsilon_{\mu}^{\dagger}
is invertible.
∎

Construction 6.11
.

Suppose
{\mathfrak{C}}
is a
{\sf C}^{*}\mathsf{Gray}
-monoid and
A\in{\mathfrak{C}}
is a unital algebra.
As in Construction
6.4
, we define the monoidal category

|A|:=\Hom_{\mathfrak{C}}(1_{\mathfrak{C}}\to A)
.

|A|
with a dagger structure given by the dagger in
\Hom_{\mathfrak{C}}(1_{\mathfrak{C}}\to A)

(As above, a vertically reflected node represents the unitary adjoint of the node).

We first prove
f^{\vee{\dagger}}=f^{{\dagger}\vee}
for all
f:a\to b
in
|A|
.
This amounts to proving the pasting diagram in Figure
3
below commutes.
Going to the right and down is
f^{\vee{\dagger}}
, and going down and then right is
f^{{\dagger}\vee}
.
The middle hexagon commutes by (
26
).
The remaining cells of the pasting diagram also commute, but for the portions of the diagram below and above the middle hexagon, we suppress canonical isomorphisms of the form
\alpha,\kappa,\lambda,\rho,\phi
, and include at most one type of interesting morphism of the form
f^{\dagger},\varepsilon,\eta
per cell of the pasting diagram.
We leave this straightforward exercise to the reader.
∎

Corollary 6.14
.

When
{\mathfrak{C}}=2\mathsf{Hilb}
and
({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})\in 2\mathsf{Hilb}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra,

(|{\mathcal{A}}|,\vee,\psi_{|{\mathcal{A}}|})
is an

{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category.
Moreover, the canonical unitary monoidal equivalence
{\mathcal{A}}\cong|{\mathcal{A}}|
is isometric.

Proof.

Recall that the canonical map
{\mathcal{A}}\to|{\mathcal{A}}|
is given by

a\mapsto(-\otimes a:H\mapsto H\otimes a)

on objects and by

(f:a\to a^{\prime})\mapsto(-\otimes f:-\otimes a\Rightarrow-\otimes a^{\prime})
.
It remains to show this equivalence is isometric from
({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})
to
(|{\mathcal{A}}|,\psi_{|{\mathcal{A}}|}\circ\tr_{R}^{\vee})
.

We begin by noticing that since
\eta_{\mu}\circ\eta_{a}\circ\eta_{\iota}
and
\eta_{\iota\otimes_{|{\mathcal{A}}|}a}
are related by a unitary (the canonical tensorator of the UAF), we have

Note that by Sub-Example
2.22
,
(\eta_{a})_{\mathbb{C}}
is the mate of
\id_{a}
under the unitary adjunction

{\mathcal{A}}({\mathbb{C}}\otimes a\to a)\cong\mathsf{Hilb}({\mathbb{C}}\to{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a)).

We can now directly use the proof of
[
HPT24
, Lem. 2.7]
and the definition of
\Psi^{2\mathsf{Hilb}}_{\mathsf{Hilb}}
in Sub-Example
4.8
:

\displaystyle\Tr^{\mathcal{A}}_{a}(f)

\displaystyle=\langle\id_{a}|f\rangle_{{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a)}

\displaystyle=\langle\mate(\id_{a})|\mate(f)\rangle_{\mathsf{Hilb}({\mathbb{C}}\to{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a))}

\displaystyle=\langle(\eta_{a})_{\mathbb{C}}|(\id_{a^{*}}\otimes f)\circ(\eta_{a})_{\mathbb{C}}\rangle_{\mathsf{Hilb}({\mathbb{C}}\to{\mathcal{A}}(a\to a))}

\displaystyle=\Tr^{\mathsf{Hilb}}_{{\mathbb{C}}}((\eta_{a})_{\mathbb{C}}^{\dagger}\circ(\id_{a^{*}}\otimes f)\circ(\eta_{a})_{\mathbb{C}})

\displaystyle=\Psi^{2\mathsf{Hilb}}_{\mathsf{Hilb}}(\eta_{a}^{\dagger}\circ(\id_{a^{*}}\otimes f)\circ\eta_{a})=\eqref{eq:FormulaForPsi|A|}.\qed

Corollary 6.16
.

When
{\mathfrak{C}}=2\mathsf{Hilb}
and
({\mathcal{A}},\Tr^{\mathcal{A}})\in 2\mathsf{Hilb}
is an
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra,
and
({\mathcal{M}},\Tr^{\mathcal{M}})
is a unital
{\mathcal{A}}
-module,

(|{\mathcal{M}}|,\Tr^{|{\mathcal{M}}|})

is a unital unitary
(|{\mathcal{A}}|,\vee,\psi_{|{\mathcal{A}}|})
-module equipped with a module trace.
Moreover, the canonical unitary
{\mathcal{A}}\cong|{\mathcal{A}}|
module equivalence
{\mathcal{M}}\cong|{\mathcal{M}}|
is isometric.

Proof.

We leave this proof to the reader, as it is almost identical to the proof of Corollary
6.14
.
∎

Proof of Theorem
E
.

Proposition
6.10
gives an assignment of objects of
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}
to objects of
\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb})
.
Additionally, a bimodule category for the
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-multifusion category is naturally a bimodule for the underlying
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebra (just by forgetting the bimodule trace).
This assembles into a 3-functor
U:{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}\to\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb})
.
By Corollaries
6.14
and
6.16
,
the 3-functor
|-|
lands in
{\sf H}^{*}\mathsf{mFC}

and the composite
|U(-)|
is equivalent to the identity.
Moreover, this equivalence is isometric on objects and 1-cells.
(Here, we use the folding trick to apply the above module result to bimodules.)
It only remains to be seen that there is a natural equivalence of 3-functors
U(|-|)\cong\id_{\mathsf{H^{*}Alg}({\mathrm{B}}2\mathsf{Hilb})}
.
This follows from Corollary
6.7
.
Notice that the unitarity conditions in Definition
6.8
are all properties, not structure, and so the equivalence
U(|{\mathcal{A}}|)\cong{\mathcal{A}}
in Corollary
6.7
is still an equivalence of
{\mathrm{H}}^{*}
-algebras.
∎
